articles.summary: Trump must accept the realities of the war if he wants a deal
articles.keyPoints:
• Trump must accept the realities of the war if he wants a deal
• Before the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. President Donald Trump had repeatedly threatened to “destroy” Iran unless it entered into a deal with the U.S. to end the war. Since the elections, in which Mr. Trump’s Republican Party suffered a massive defeat , the U.S. President appears to have toned down his rhetoric. Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. The U.S. and Israel carried out heavy bombing for 40 days but achieved none of their declared objectives. There is no guarantee that another round of strikes would force Iran to change its position. And the war, as the midterm results show, remains very unpopular in America.
• Mr. Trump has only himself, and Benjamin Netanyahu, to blame for the predicament he is in. He is the one who sabotaged a functioning Obama-era nuclear deal in 2018 that had denied Iran a path towards the nuclear bomb. Mr. Trump joined Israel’s unprovoked war on Iran in June 2025 and declared that he had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear programme. And the same Mr. Trump started the current war, just eight months later, over the same nuclear programme. The Iranian state has survived, though Iranians are facing enormous economic woes. Tehran shut the Strait of Hormuz, pumping up global energy prices. Iran’s counterattacks have either destroyed or damaged America’s bases in the Persian Gulf. High oil prices and inflation turned the American electorate against the Republican party, while in Israel, Mr. Netanyahu, despite war rhetoric and racist attacks on the country’s Arab minorities, lost the governing majority. The setbacks are there for anyone to see. Yet, Mr. Trump does not seem to have grasped the seriousness of the situation. His no-war, no-deal approach r isks a resumption of hostilities as Iran has pledged to break the siege. The U.S. has few clear military options unless it is prepared to launch a ground invasion, which would be disastrous. A more rational way forward is to end the war through diplomacy. But for that, Mr. Trump must first accept the strategic reality that he has lost the war.

fullParagraphs: The Congress should scale down its ambition while seeking an alliance with the SP

As Uttar Pradesh heads to the polls in early 2027, a familiar seat-sharing tussle has emerged within the Opposition. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress share an understanding forged during the Lok Sabha elections that earned them a good share of the State’s seats, but the Congress is now reportedly seeking 181 seats , nearly 45% of the 403 Assembly constituencies. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. With discontent rising against the BJP, which still occupies a hegemonic position in the party system , the Opposition feels a wind behind its sails, and its major parties agree that the only way to take on the BJP is a formidable coalition with a compelling, unified message. But the Congress’s attempt to rebuild itself in the Hindi heartland and in States where it once held sway has strained that unity. In Bihar, the Mahagathbandhan failed to reap the benefits of anti-incumbency against the Janata Dal (United)-BJP alliance, partly because it could not tap the full support of the social forces behind the Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Congress, and partly because the Congress took too long to settle seat-sharing for the campaigns to gel. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners.

Uttar Pradesh need not go the same way. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. A well-targeted 100 or so seats would make for a more coherent campaign and a better showing alongside the SP.

articles.title: Jharkhand SIR: Final BLO meetings at poll stations on November 18
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jharkhand CEO K Ravi Kumar appeals to all eligible Indian citizens in the state to ensure their names are included in the electoral roll by taking part in Ek Aur Avsar (One More Opportunity) camps

Jharkhand Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) K. Ravi Kumar on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) appealed to all eligible Indian citizens in the State to ensure their names are included in the electoral roll being published under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

Speaking to the media in Ranchi, Mr. Ravi asserted that an “Ek Aur Avsar” (One More Opportunity) camp will be held on November 18 at all polling stations in the State, from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., where meetings of BLOs (Booth Level Officers) and BLAs-2 (Booth Level Agents-2) will take place in the form of a “Chunav Pathshala” (Electoral Awareness Session).

He pointed out that the objective of this special initiative is to provide one additional opportunity for any eligible Indian citizen who, for various reasons, has not yet had their name added to the electoral roll.

Mr. Ravi explained that the camps will focus primarily on three key areas. First, the Election Commission of India (ECI) is republishing the ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead, or Duplicate) list at all polling stations. If any eligible Indian citizen has been included in this list, they may follow the prescribed procedure to submit Form-6 or an enumeration form.

Second, lists of voters in categories such as “No Mapping” or those with “Logical Discrepancies”—who have failed to provide the necessary documentation despite receiving two notices from the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) and undergoing a door-to-door verification process—will be made available at the respective polling stations.

Third, efforts are being made to identify eligible Indian citizens who will have turned 18 by October 1, 2026, but who have not yet registered their names in the electoral roll for their respective polling stations. Eligible Indian citizens will be able to have their names included in the electoral roll by submitting Form 6.

The CEO said that this is the sixth and final BLO-BLA-2 meeting being held under the ongoing SIR process in Jharkhand. He urged all eligible citizens in the state to take advantage of this opportunity and get their names added to the electoral roll, ensuring that no eligible Indian citizen remains excluded.

The ECI has already extended the deadline for final publication of electoral rolls in Jharkhand under the SIR to November 30. The final publication was initially scheduled for October 7 and was later extended to October 19 before being revised.

articles.title: Construction activities on Kaziranga wildlife corridors flagged
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: An Eastern Assam-based environment activist writes to the Supreme Court-constituted Central Empowered Committee, highlighting the concerns

An eastern Assam-based environmental activist has reminded the Supreme Court–constituted Central Empowered Committee (CEC) to continue construction activities on the wildlife corridors of Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve.

Kaziranga has nine notified wildlife corridors and several dandis or animal pathways. Animals use these corridors and dandis mostly to escape to the hills of Karbi Anglong district when the park is flooded during the monsoon months.

In a letter to the CEC’s Member-Secretary on November 16, Rohit Choudhury said he had brought such construction activities to the notice of the Committee on May 11. He lamented the lack of action against these activities, violating the Supreme Court’s April 2019 order.

“We order that all kinds of mining and related activities along the aforesaid Kaziranga National Park area and in the entire catchment area of rivers, streams and rivulets originating in the Karbi Anglong Hill ranges and flowing into Kaziranga National Park, including the Tiger Reserve, are restrained. No new construction shall be permitted on private lands which form part of the nine identified animal corridors,” the apex court’s order read.

“Despite this clear and categorical prohibition, the Government of Assam has displayed a disturbing disregard for the mandate of the Supreme Court by permitting and facilitating unlawful construction activities within these ecologically sensitive wildlife corridors,” Mr. Choudhury wrote.

He reminded the CEC of photographic evidence of a building under construction on the Haldhibari Wildlife Corridor attached to his May 11 letter. “The construction activity was allowed to proceed unabated and has now reached an advanced stage of completion,” he wrote, attaching recent photographs of the construction site.

Mr. Choudhury said the CEC’s inability to take up the matter six months ago “effectively afforded the concerned authorities sufficient time to continue and substantially complete the illegal construction”.
He said such delays in addressing matters of grave environmental significance seriously undermine the purpose and efficacy of the CEC’s mandate.
The activist further said the Assam Government did not inform the Supreme Court of any instance of violation of its April 12, 2019, order for necessary action.

“This persistent failure of enforcement has emboldened continued violations and weakened the protection envisaged by the Supreme Court,” he said, urging the CEC to recommend contempt proceedings against the officials responsible for permitting, facilitating or failing to prevent these blatant violations of the court’s binding directions.

articles.title: Kedarnath generates 73 tonnes of waste during 2026 Char Dham Yatra
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Around 65.65 lakh pilgrims visit four Char Dham shrines and Hemkund Sahib in 2026 as Badrinath portals close for winter

Pilgrims visiting the Kedarnath shrine generated 73 tonnes of waste during the 2026 Char Dham Yatra, more than three times the amount recorded last year. The yatra, which ended on Monday (November 16, 2026) with the closure of the Badrinath shrine portals, witnessed a record 65.65 lakh pilgrims this year.
According to data shared by the civic body at Kedarnath, the 73 tonnes of waste comprised plastic bottles, food packets, Tetra Pak, and cardboard.
Neeraj Kukreti, an official of the Kedarnath Nagar Panchayat, told The Hindu that waste generation this year was more than three times the 21.40 tonnes recorded in 2025.
The waste generated in Kedarnath stood at 26.10 tonnes in 2024 and 32.58 tonnes in 2023, he added.

To help manage the waste buildup near the temple, the district administration launched the ‘Carry Me Back’ initiative in June. The drive mobilised over 6,000 pilgrims to carry 14 tonnes of waste down to a collection point, from where it was sent for segregation and disposal.”

The increase in waste generation comes amid a broader rise in pilgrim numbers across Uttarakhand’s Char Dham circuit, according to a comparative analysis released by the Dehradun-based SDC Foundation.

Prepared by Anoop Nautiyal and Praveen Upreti, the study found that 65.65 lakh pilgrims visited the four Char Dham shrines — Kedarnath, Badrinath, Gangotri and Yamunotri — and Hemkund Sahib in 2026, registering a 29% increase over 51.07 lakh in 2025. The pilgrimage season extended from mid-April to mid-November.

Kedarnath recorded 19,33,138 pilgrims, a 9% rise over the previous year. However, its average daily footfall declined by around 6%, from 10,113 pilgrims in 2025 to 9,476 in 2026. The foundation attributed the higher cumulative numbers partly to a longer pilgrimage season and fewer weather-related disruptions. Kedarnath remained operational for 204 days, compared with 175 days last year.

The SDC Foundation report also flagged concerns over pilgrim safety, recording 297 fatalities across the five shrines in 2026, compared with 182 in 2025. Health-related natural deaths alone increased by 81%, from 159 to 288, with Kedarnath accounting for 142 such deaths.

Vehicle movement during the Char Dham Yatra also witnessed a significant rise, increasing from 5,14,016 in 2025 to 6,68,877 in 2026 (till November 14). This represents an increase of 1,54,861 vehicles, or more than 30% over the previous year.

articles.title: Ruckus erupts between SFI activists and police over setting up bookstalls near Calcutta University
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The SFI leaders said they sought permission from the Kolkata Police to set up a bookstall on the College Street footpath, but police refused on November 16 evening, saying it could disrupt traffic

A ruckus erupted between supporters of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI), the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist), and police near the University of Kolkata for setting up a book stall. After the clash, police detained several SFI supporters, including the SFI State secretary, Debanjan Dey.

The SFI leadership said that they sought permission from the Kolkata Police to set up a book stall at a makeshift stall on the footpath of College Street. However, the police refused to grant permission on Monday evening, stating that it might disrupt traffic. The book stall was part of a three-day campaign, “Sangrami Boipotro”, by the party. It was supposed to be inaugurated by the Left Front chairman, Biman Bose, on Tuesday evening.

“We have permission from the Kolkata Municipal Corporation and Jorasanko Police Station for a period of five years to set up bookstalls at College Street. Necessary tax was also paid to the concerned authorities. We have been setting up such stalls for the last four years. Our plan was to do the same this year too. But the Kolkata Police have now refused to allow us anymore,” said Mr. Dey to the media persons

The protesters said that a few police vans had already been stationed on College Street since Monday night. When they began preparing to set up the stalls on Tuesday morning, the police stopped them and said that no book stalls could be organised in the area.

The situation escalated when they blocked College Street and staged a sit-in. They laid out a sheet on the tram line in the middle of the road and began selling their books. They also invited the police to buy books for their children. It immediately resulted in a clash with the police. The police were seen using mild force to disrupt the protesters and clear the road. Several activists, including Mr. Dey, Subhadeep Bandyopadhyay, Didhiti Roy, and Haseeb Hossain, have been detained.

“A heavy police force was deployed across College Street on Tuesday only to stop us selling some books. They have assaulted the students who have been fighting for the books. It is now clear that the government has declared war against the books. They want to destroy the culture and tradition of Bengal. We will have to fight the battle with books only against them,” said Mr. Dey after the detention.
Following the development, the left student union also organised a rally in the evening at the Mahabodhi Society and demanded the immediate release of the detained students.

The dispute over the book stalls set up by the Left parties began during Durga Puja. Police and civic bodies demolished several stalls set up by the parties across Kolkata. In Jadavpur, a bulldozer was also brought in to dismantle a stall, sparking a huge political controversy. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had described Left party supporters as “atheist” and declared that they would not be allowed to set up their book stalls near puja pandals, where such stalls have been a fixture for decades.

articles.title: U.K. hands NATO-assigned American soldier accused of Russia spying to U.S.
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A U.S. Army official has named the detained soldier as 41-year-old Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner

A senior American soldier assigned to NATO who was arrested in Britain last week on suspicion of spying for Russia has been transferred to U.S. military custody, U.K. police said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

The espionage case, the latest involving suspected Kremlin agents in Britain and elsewhere in Europe, comes amid heightened tensions between Moscow and various European capitals after Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
It also follows recent security scares at two British air force bases hosting the U.S. military, with officials accusing Iran of involvement in plots to target them.
A U.S. Army official has named the detained soldier as 41-year-old Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner.

Held in British police custody since his November 10 arrest near Gloucester, southwest England, he was handed to the US military “over suspected national security and espionage allegations”, U.K. Counter Terrorism Policing said.

Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor said the decision to “pass the investigation to them to progress” followed an extensive probe by his counter-terror unit and subsequent discussions between British prosecutors and “American partners”.
FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement that the unnamed Army officer was in U.S. custody after “an espionage investigation”.
He noted it had involved “close cooperation” between the FBI’s Philadelphia field office and various other US and UK law enforcement and intelligence agencies.
“Together we worked to identify a potential threat to national security and take swift action,” Mr. Patel added.

A senior NATO military official last week confirmed that the arrested soldier had been assigned to its Allied Rapid Reaction Corps (ARRC), the alliance’s 20-nation, high-readiness force led by the British Army.

articles.title: Earthshot Prize: Climate action needs innovation, global cooperation, say leaders on green carpet in Mumbai
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Maharashtra Environment and Climate Change Minister Pankaja Munde called for global cooperation to protect the planet for future generations

Global leaders, business executives, and celebrities called for greater investment in environmental innovations and collective action against climate change as they gathered on the green carpet ahead of the Earthshot Prize Awards in Mumbai on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).
Among those attending were former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern, Serum Institute of India CEO Adar Poonawalla, filmmaker Karan Johar, and Maharashtra Environment Minister Pankaja Mund.
Speaking to reporters, Mr. Poonawalla emphasised the importance of supporting environmental innovations and helping them attract investment.

“Prevention is better than cure—that’s what we believe at Serum Institute,” he said, explaining the company’s partnership with the Earthshot Prize. He added that the initiative would help innovators connect with investors and scale up technologies capable of addressing environmental challenges.
Ms. Ardern welcomed the awards to Mumbai, highlighting India’s record of producing the highest number of Earthshot finalists and winners.

“The Earthshot Prize is showcasing responses to that crisis to demonstrate that things are happening and innovation is available, we just need to scale it up with speed,” she said, referring to the climate crisis.

Coral Pasisi, president of Tofia, Niue, highlighted Indigenous-led ocean conservation efforts. “We’re protecting one of the largest areas of ocean on the planet. And we developed a sustainable financing mechanism that’s driven by Indigenous people,” she said, stressing the need for international support.

Maharashtra Environment and Climate Change Minister Pankaja Munde called for global cooperation to protect the planet for future generations. She expressed concern that rapid urbanisation and industrialisation had drowned out natural sounds, including birdsong and flowing water, and urged people to protect forests and biodiversity.
Filmmaker Karan Johar praised Prince William’s environmental commitment, describing him as a “climate warrior” who empowered innovators through the Earthshot Prize.

Actor Sonam Kapoor emphasised that environmental responsibility extended beyond public statements. Speaking about her children, she said individuals and governments needed to take concrete steps to protect the environment for future generations.

articles.title: Fearmongering around fake drugs
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: As per the last National Drug Survey published in 2017, the volume of counterfeit drugs in the Indian market detected in the survey was at a negligible 0.0245%

Recent news from Karnataka regarding the seizure of fake cancer drugs from a licensed distributor during a raid has understandably sparked concerns. Counterfeit drugs for serious conditions like cancer are a sensational and emotive issue, often provoking a demand for severe action, including death sentences for those involved in the distribution.

However, in this case, there is a serious reason to doubt the authenticity of the news reports about the recent seizure since the Government of Karnataka has not confirmed that indeed counterfeit cancer drugs were seized in the raid. While a purported list of the drugs seized was circulated on social media, it only contained antibiotics, not cancer drugs. The silence of the State Health Department on the news reports about the counterfeit drugs is insensitive to the dread and uncertainty being faced by patients receiving cancer treatment, not to mention the doubts of those wondering whether they lost their loved ones to cancer because of counterfeit drugs. The Department should clear the air on the matter by issuing a press release or holding a press conference. If counterfeit cancer drugs were indeed seized, the government should release the names of the drugs and the hospitals possibly affected. If not, it should at least communicate the same to the public. Letting the uncertainty hang without authoritative answers is not in public interest.
Science, Space & Environment Report: Fearmongering around fake drugs. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

The Department should clear the air on the matter by issuing a press release or holding a press conference. If counterfeit cancer drugs were indeed seized, the government should release the names of the drugs and the hospitals possibly affected. articles.title: Transgender rights, healthcare should not be compromised
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Clinical understanding of the care needs of a transgender person remains rudimentary in India. Doctors, nurses, receptionists, security staff and hospital administrators need to be trained in basic transgender health.

Parliament passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026 earlier this year. The new Act represents a significant shift from the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019. The 2026 amendment removes the principle of self-identification and demands a medical board’s recommendation; a selection from prescribed categories; and certification by a District Magistrate. It fundamentally changes legal recognition for transgender persons from self-identification to medical assessment. While the 2026 Act does increase protection, it changes the philosophical foundation of transgender rights — from recognition based substantially on autonomy and self-identification towards recognition mediated by medical and administrative authorities.

The definition of “transgender” as introduced in the Amendment Act is in contradiction to established international evidence and guidelines laid down in the World Health Organization ICD-11 and the World Professional Association for Transgender Health Standards of Care Version 8.

articles.title: Prince William says Gen Z is the torchbearer of the global movement for change
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Himalayan Kingdom of Bhutan, Mahindra Last Mile Mobility among the five winners of Earthshot Prize

Young people from around the world are not waiting for someone else to find the solution, they are the torchbearers of the global movement for change, Britain’s Prince William said in Mumbai on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).
He was speaking at the 2026 Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony, which was held in India for the first time.

“India is a nation of extraordinary innovation, ambition, facing immense environmental pressures, yet moving ahead with determination. Not because the challenge is simple, not because the path is easy. But because millions of people have decided that progress simply cannot wait,” said Prince William.
Winners of the Earthshot Prize award were declared under five categories in a glittering ceremony. The awardees include the Himalayan Kingdom of Bhutan and Mahindra Last Mile Mobility.
“They [Gen Z] are bringing fresh ideas and showing what is possible when optimism is matched with action. Their ideas, their energy, and their determination are helping to shape the future,” he said.
During his address, Prince William reflected on the achievements of this year’s finalists and the growing global movement behind environmental innovation.
The ceremony was attended by environmental innovators, philanthropists, business leaders, government representatives and global figures from sport, entertainment and culture.
Mahindra Last Mile Mobility won the Earthshot Prize in the ‘Clean Our Air’ category. Accepting the award, the company’s CEO, Suman Mishra, said it showed how urgent optimism worked.
The company has won 1 million pounds for its efforts, due to which 33 per cent of India’s three-wheelers are now electric.

articles.title: Clear the path: On SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India should use multilateral fora to advance bilateral cooperation

While maintaining its hard stance on cross-border terrorism, India has an opportunity to recognise that many of its other interests still merit sustained cooperation with Pakistan as the latter’s climate minister Musadik Masood Malik prepares to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. India’s official position since the Pahalgam attack and the ensuing confrontations along the border is that terrorism and bilateral talks cannot coexist. A month later, Prime Minister Narendra Modi signalled that India’s relations with Pakistan would remain subordinate to its demands on cross-border terrorism by extending the condition to trade and water. South Asia is already one of the least economically integrated regions worldwide, with intra-regional trade at around 5%, and, as Chatham House has inferred, strained ties between India and its neighbours have created diplomatic vacuums that Beijing has taken advantage of through trilateral and regional groupings. Now, by inviting all SCO members to the national capital and participating in meetings ahead of the August 2027 Islamabad Summit, New Delhi has shown some maturity as a convening power. Islamabad is also being pragmatic in keeping channels open during its SCO chairmanship by participating in an initiative championed by Mr. Modi.

The pursuit of regionwide water security remains particularly fluid, with India seemingly overlooking the fact that it is upstream of Pakistan and Bangladesh and downstream of China. After India stopped sharing routine hydrological data of the Indus river and approved the Chenab-Beas link tunnel project, Mr. Malik fanned the flames saying Pakistan would “cut off those hands” seeking to restrict its share of the water. Yet China has now restricted the same data vis-à-vis the Brahmaputra while it builds the Medog mega-dam in Tibet. India has also protested the proposed Padma Barrage in Bangladesh, which has been increasing its alignment with China, echoing India building the Farakka Barrage over East Pakistan’s objections in 1961. Climate change is rendering cooperation more essential to manage the integrity of contested geographies, the willingness of border populations to engage, and the potential to generate hydroelectric power. New Delhi should retreat from the notion that working together on the Indus will be a concession to Islamabad and see in the Dialogue an opportunity to restore the necessary channels. Suspending ties may communicate political resolve but will not diminish terrorists’ capabilities in the region or improve India’s security. It has already compromised India’s ambitions to regional leadership, which require the ability to keep engaging even with difficult neighbours. India should go beyond using multilateral fora to assert its national position and start identifying areas where bilateral cooperation serves its interests, including with Pakistan.

articles.title: Outlook outage: On Microsoft and dangers of centralising digital systems
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The dangers of centralising the internet’s architecture are now clear

Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

The dangers of centralising the internet’s architecture are now clear

Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

articles.title: Brace for impact: On rising inflation and external factors
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: High inflation due to external factors could soon exacerbate economic pain

India’s much-hyped domestic economic resilience is set to be tested over the next few months as external factors start to impose inescapable pressures. A case in point is inflation. The latest data on retail inflation show that it crossed the Reserve Bank of India’s 6% upper comfort limit in October 2026. According to economists, this is likely to continue through the third quarter of this financial year, which means at least two more months of high inflation. Agricultural shortfalls brought on by a patchy and deficient monsoon have meant that food inflation rose sharply to 8.5% in October 2026. Elevated fuel prices meant that inflation in the transport category also rose sharply. What is worse is that high inflation is spreading to almost every aspect of a household’s day-to-day needs. In fact, the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) data show that 10 of the 12 major categories saw inflation in October, hitting their highest levels recorded in the new series of the index. So, things such as clothing, footwear, housing, furnishings, and services such as healthcare, education, communication, recreation, and restaurant and hospitality are not only getting more expensive, but they are doing so at an accelerating rate. This would have been bad enough had wages been increasing in real terms. Yet, the latest research by Data for India on the country’s official wage statistics shows that, while nominal wages doubled from 2012 to 2024, they actually fell 4% over the same period after adjusting for inflation. And this is sharper for high-skilled and high-earning workers. Lower wage earners saw marginal increases over this period. While this is of some comfort, it is the higher wage earners that drive consumption in an economy. Real wage contraction for them, which is likely to have worsened in 2026, will hit consumption levels and private investment.

Further, there is strong evidence to suggest that the official inflation metrics are not capturing the full extent of rising prices. Data on cash with the public and UPI transactions show the value of both has been growing in double digits over the last year and more, significantly outpacing nominal GDP growth. This either suggests that the informal economy is far larger than earlier thought or, more likely, that inflation is well above what the official figures are being able to capture. Unfortunately, there are no real magic-wand fixes to this situation. Inflation is largely beyond the government’s control, and wage growth cannot happen overnight. The only way forward is to continue trying to spur sector-specific growth and warn people of the impending storm.

articles.title: Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 17 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

articles.title: BJP holds key party meeting in Mathura for Assembly polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The party announced the meeting to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and public welfare benefits, while also outlining electoral strategy and caste-based outreach

Senior BJP leaders from Uttar Pradesh, including Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, attended a key meeting at the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Cow Research Institute in Parkham, Mathura, to discuss strategy for the upcoming U.P. Assembly polls.

The party announced the meeting to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and public welfare benefits, while also outlining electoral strategy and caste-based outreach to counter the Opposition’s renewed pitch.

“One goal, one idea... BJP government again for the third time... Today, in Mathura, the birthplace of Lord Krishna, I participated in a planning meeting with National General Secretary (Organisation) B.L. Santosh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, and BJP Uttar Pradesh Incharge Shri Vinod Tawde,” wrote Pankaj Chaudhary, U.P. BJP president, on X.

“In the meeting, various important topics, including upcoming organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and providing benefits of public welfare schemes to every household, were discussed in detail. On this occasion, National General Secretary Irani, Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Keshav Prasad Maurya ji and Shri Brajesh Pathak, co-incharges of BJP Uttar Pradesh, Ministers of the State Government, public representatives, and state officials were present,” he added.

State Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya said the construction of a grand temple at Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura will be a major poll issue in the 2027 U.P. elections, and that a grand Krishna temple will be built—through the courts or mutual dialogue, as with Ayodhya.
“If Akhilesh Yadav wants to join us in kar seva, we will take him along too to build a grand temple of Lord Krishna,” said the Deputy CM.

The meeting in Mathura is also significant amid the BJP’s emphasis on Mathura and western Uttar Pradesh. “The BJP holds meetings regularly to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment and other issues. Reach out to various sections of society is also part of our work,” said Dinesh Dubey, a senior BJP leader based in Lucknow.

Asad Rizvi, a political analyst based in Lucknow, said, “the meeting is significant as it is organised only a few months before the Assembly elections. Amid the main Opposition parties (the Samajwadi Party-Congress) pushing backwards, Scheduled Castes (SCs), Brahmins and marginalised groups through the PDA plank, the BJP will be recalibrating their policies and making a renewed effort towards them. ”

The SP president Akhilesh Yadav in a cryptic statement urged the BJP leaders to take a dip in the Yamuna and sip its water before starting the event. “I request them to take a dip in the Yamuna and sip its water before starting the event. It will be auspicious. If they fall ill, call a good doctor,” said Mr. Yadav.

articles.title: Tribute to Kartar Singh Sarabha, Punjab free from drugs and unemployment, says CM Mann
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision

Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann said on Monday (November 16, 2026) that the greatest tribute to the 19-year-old revolutionary and freedom fighter Kartar Singh Sarabha is to fulfil his dream of a Punjab free from drugs, unemployment, and injustice.

He was speaking after paying tribute to Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha on his 111th martyrdom anniversary at his native village, Sarabha, in Ludhiana district. The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision.

“Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha embraced the gallows at the tender age of just 19, proving that courage, conviction and love for the motherland know no age. At a time when youngsters today are planning their futures, this great revolutionary was planning the liberation of the country. He sacrificed his youth, dreams and ultimately his life for our freedom,” he said.

“On November 16, 1915, Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha was hanged at Lahore Central Jail along with six other revolutionaries in the First Lahore Conspiracy Case. His fearless commitment to the freedom of the country remains a shining example of patriotism and selflessness,” he added.

As the Punjab 2027 Assembly election approaches, the drug menace has once again become a central campaign issue. In the run-up to the Assembly polls, the major political parties in the fray—the Congress, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), and the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)—are making the drug menace a key plank of their campaigns.

While the ruling party has been asserting that eradicating drugs is its “biggest priority,” the Opposition parties have accused the AAP of failing to curb the drug menace and instead patronising the drug trade.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision

Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann said on Monday (November 16, 2026) that the greatest tribute to the 19-year-old revolutionary and freedom fighter Kartar Singh Sarabha is to fulfil his dream of a Punjab free from drugs, unemployment, and injustice.

He was speaking after paying tribute to Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha on his 111th martyrdom anniversary at his native village, Sarabha, in Ludhiana district. The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision.

“Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha embraced the gallows at the tender age of just 19, proving that courage, conviction and love for the motherland know no age. At a time when youngsters today are planning their futures, this great revolutionary was planning the liberation of the country. He sacrificed his youth, dreams and ultimately his life for our freedom,” he said.

“On November 16, 1915, Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha was hanged at Lahore Central Jail along with six other revolutionaries in the First Lahore Conspiracy Case. His fearless commitment to the freedom of the country remains a shining example of patriotism and selflessness,” he added.

As the Punjab 2027 Assembly election approaches, the drug menace has once again become a central campaign issue. In the run-up to the Assembly polls, the major political parties in the fray—the Congress, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), and the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)—are making the drug menace a key plank of their campaigns.

While the ruling party has been asserting that eradicating drugs is its “biggest priority,” the Opposition parties have accused the AAP of failing to curb the drug menace and instead patronising the drug trade.

articles.title: Kishtwar killings aftermath: Remarks by Congress’ Karra, BJP’s Parihar spark protests in J&K
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Karra said that “two SPOs were killed by the Army in a mistaken-identity case on November 11”, while senior BJP leader Sharma said, “Congress is spreading misleading information to shift blame from terrorists to security forces”

Two separate remarks made by J&K Pradesh Congress Committee (JKPCC) president Tariq Hameed Karra and BJP legislator Shagun Parihar in the aftermath of the killing of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) in Kishtwar on Monday (November 16, 2026) sparked protests from different quarters.

In response to the statement by Mr. Karra that “two SPOs were killed reportedly by the Army in a mistaken identity case on November 11”, senior BJP leader and Leader of Opposition (LoP) Sunil Sharma said, “The Congress is spreading misleading information to shift the blame from terrorists to our security forces. The SPOs were on duty and travelling to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah to relieve the jawans posted there. Calling two martyrs hunters is an insult to their sacrifice and to their grieving families.”
He demanded that Mr. Karra “immediately withdraw the remarks and apologise to the martyrs’ families, the J&K Police and the Indian Army”.

Scores of members of the BJP and BJP-affiliated organisations held street protests against Mr. Karra and the Congress in Jammu. Members of the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) also burn an effigy of Mr. Karra as a mark of protest.

BJYM leader Arun Prabhat, while condemning the statement of Mr. Karra, said, “It shows the hearts of Congress beat for Pakistan. The conspirators should face action. In case of any role of mosques, such places too should face action.”

Mr. Prabhat was seconding the controversial remarks of Ms. Parihar of the BJP, who claimed “announcements were made from the mosques in Kishtwar’s Dachhan area to identify the targets” allegedly ahead of the killings of two SPOs on November 11.

However, several religious organisations, including the Anjuman Islamia Bhaderwah and Kishtwar, in the Chenab Valley condemned the statement of Ms. Parihar and denied any role of mosques in the latest attack on the policemen. Ruling National Conference (NC) legislator Tanvir Sadiq said the BJP must be “held accountable for its MLA’s deeply irresponsible and inflammatory allegations against a mosque in Jammu”.

“Making communal allegations in the aftermath of a tragic killing is utterly unacceptable. The BJP leadership cannot hide behind silence or pretend this is an isolated matter. It must unequivocally condemn these remarks and issue an unconditional public apology. Stop playing with the communal harmony of J&K,” said Mr. Sadiq.

A spokesman of the All J&K Shia Association said the organisation “strongly condemn Ms. Parihar’s attempt to drag a mosque into the tragic killing of our brave SPOs”. “Terrorists are enemies of all humanity and terrorism has no religion. Unsubstantiated claims against a place of worship only weaken our fight against terror,” said the Association.
Jammu and Kashmir / Indian National Congress / Bharatiya Janata Party

articles.title: Christian community seeks West Bengal CM’s intervention over targeted attacks ahead of Christmas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bishop of Calcutta Reverend Paritosh Canning ruled out claims of religious conversion by institutions affiliated with the Churches of North India

Ahead of the upcoming Christmas festivities, the representatives of Christian communities in West Bengal have expressed concerns about the rising attacks on churches across several districts in the State and have sought intervention from Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari.

During a press conference addressed by the Bengal Christian Council (a cluster body for Protestant churches), the Bishop of Calcutta, Reverend Paritosh Canning, said that the concerns of the people of the community are not without reason.

“West Bengal has traditionally been a land of communal harmony, where people belonging to different faiths and communities have coexisted in peace, mutual respect, and brotherhood. With Christmas approaching, the apprehensions of the Christian community have become particularly serious. However, the prevailing atmosphere of insecurity has raised genuine concerns about whether Christians will be able to observe their religious services and celebrate festivals without fear or disruption,” the bishop said, speaking to media persons.

He added that such incidents have increased since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government came to power in West Bengal in May 2026. Attacks have been reported across several districts in South Bengal, on both banks of the Hooghly River, including South 24 Parganas, North 24 Parganas, Purba Medinipur, and Paschim Medinipur, among others.

Bishop Canning said that there are allegations of religious conversions in the churches, adding that “we can confirm that no conversion takes place at the churches operating under the Churches of North India.”
“All the minority communities used to live peacefully under the previous governments. However, it is not clear who the attackers are or why they are doing this,” he said.

In another development, representatives of Bangiya Christiya Pariseba (BCP) held a meeting in response to remarks by West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya. The State BJP president had on Sunday said that religious conversions are taking place across districts in West Bengal and issued a warning to Christian missionary schools in the State, claiming that they are targeting teachers wearing saffron sarees.

The Archbishop of Calcutta (Roman Catholic), Reverend Elius Frank, also participated in a meeting organised by BCP, though he did not speak to the media. In a letter addressed to Samik Bhattacharya, Herod Mullick, the founder-secretary of BCP, said that “if any institution or individual is found guilty of illegal or forced religious conversion through greed or deception, we strongly condemn such actions and stand firmly against them.”

“However, making broad, unsubstantiated generalisations without naming specific individuals or institutions unfairly casts a shadow of suspicion over the entire Christian community and the more than 800 educational institutions we operate across West Bengal,” the letter added.

articles.title: Site inspection held for key Goshree-Mamangalam traffic corridor in Keralam’s Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Developing the stretch into a major traffic corridor is expected to help resolve the city’s persistent traffic bottlenecks to a great extent and ease the existing pressure on several roads

People’s representatives and officials on Monday conducted a site inspection for the proposed Goshree-Mamangalam road development project, which is expected to provide major relief from traffic woes in Kochi.

The project is critical to improving the overall traffic system in the city and enhancing connectivity between various points. The demand for the proposed road dates back more than 30 years. Developing this stretch into a major traffic corridor is expected to help resolve the city’s persistent traffic bottlenecks to a great extent and ease the existing pressure on several roads.

A sum of ₹1 crore was earmarked for the development of Goshree Bridge and Goshree-Mamangalam Road in the last State Budget following interventions by Hibi Eden MP, MLAs T.J. Vinod and Uma Thomas, and Mayor V.K. Minimol. The allocation was intended for conducting a traffic study, demarcating the alignment, and completing the survey. An action plan will be formulated based on scientific studies and survey findings.

Initially, the Goshree-Mamangalam road was proposed to be developed at 22 metres. However, during the tenure of the previous Kochi Corporation council, the width was scaled down to 15 metres in the 2024 Master Plan, which was subsequently approved by the State government. Based on this, follow-up measures are now being planned.

Coordination among various departments is essential, as several roads within the Kochi Corporation limits form part of the project. Accordingly, the PWD (Roads) will be entrusted with conducting the traffic study, carrying out the survey and preparing a detailed project report. This is expected to facilitate the efficient and time-bound execution of the project through coordinated efforts by the Corporation and the PWD.

The delegation assessed the existing condition of roads proposed to be included in the project, nature of traffic movement, development potential, and the role of the departments concerned. This is expected to aid the coordination of the proposed traffic study, survey, and subsequent follow-up measures.
MLAs T.J. Vinod and Uma Thomas, Mayor V.K. Minimol, and deputy mayor V.R. Sudheer were among those who participated in the inspection.

articles.title: A poverty line that falls short
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Reliable poverty estimates are not just for academic purposes. India has made real progress, but without a credible benchmark, it is hard to say how much, or how much remains to be done

There is no serious doubt that poverty in India has fallen sharply over the past decade. However, researchers and policymakers cannot agree on how many are still poor. Depending on the estimate, the share ranges from about 5% to more than 26%. Take the recent World Bank report. At its international line of $3 a day (2021 PPP), 2.6% of Indians were poor in 2022-23. Raise the line to $4.20, the bank’s benchmark for lower middle-income countries, and the figure jumps to around 16.1%. Same country, same year. Only the yardstick changed. A low level of extreme poverty does not necessarily mean poverty is not still a major issue. Where you draw the line decides how much economic insecurity you see.

India’s own figures tell a similar convoluted story. For example, SBI Research (2025) takes the Tendulkar line of 2009, adjusts it for inflation, and gets poverty of 7.2% in rural India and 4.6% in urban India for 2022-23. Rangarajan and Dev (2014), using an inflation-adjusted version of the Rangarajan Committee line, arrive at 10.8%. Further, Sethu, Surya and Ruthu (2024), who rebuild the Rangarajan method from the latest consumption survey, report 26.4%. Most of that gap boils down to the lines themselves: SBI’s Tendulkar-based lines use, after adjusting for inflation, about ₹1,632 a month per person in rural areas and ₹1,944 in urban areas. In contrast, Sethu et al. use much higher thresholds of ₹2,515 and ₹3,639. And the outcomes are obvious: Higher lines, higher poverty. Method matters too. One camp takes an old line and adjusts it for inflation. The other reconstructs the line from spending patterns in the new survey. Both have limitations, and they are answering different questions.
Macroeconomic & Financial Update: A poverty line that falls short. This development reflects key trends in India's fiscal roadmap, monetary policy transmission, and banking sector resilience.

fullParagraphs: Bank of America, Chase, J.P. Morgan, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Zelle were listed by users as down or experiencing issues, according to the website downdetector.com
Customers reported difficulty accessing the online accounts at some of the U.S.’ largest banks on Monday (November 16, 2026).
Bank of America, Chase, J.P. Morgan, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Zelle were listed by users as down or experiencing issues, according to the website downdetector.com.
Chase Bank’s services are experiencing a technical bug issue, not a cyber issue, a spokesperson said Monday (November 16, 2026).

“Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete but customers still have access to their accounts and funds,” a Chase spokesperson said in a statement. “We are working to resolve this as quickly as possible.”
The reports follow a major outage by Microsoft that began on Friday (November 13, 2026) and lasted for hours, which impacted services including Outlook, Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.
Some Chase customers received a message that said, “Some services aren’t available. We’re working on them. Please try back later.”

articles.title: ASEAN Summit LIVE updates: PM Modi to participate in ASEAN-India Summit; Quad meeting likely after President Trump arrives
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In the first Quad Summit since 2024, PM Modi is expected to meet U.S. President Trump, Japanese PM Takaichi and Australian PM Albanese
“India, ASEAN represent around one-fourth of global population; it is important to decide our future by cooperation; not by competition,” PM Modi said in the India-ASEAN Summit in Manila today.
“We believe that India’s development and ASEAN’s prosperity are deeply interconnected,” he added.

The Embassy of India in Manila will resume all regular consular services, passport applications and visa processing from Wednesday, following a temporary suspension in view of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and East Asia Summit.

According to the earlier advisory, the closure was in accordance with Proclamation No. 1447 issued by the Government of the Republic of the Philippines, declaring special non-working days in the National Capital Region (NCR) for the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits.

Joint Statement of the 29th ASEAN-Japan Summit on Realising Economic Resilience was adopted today in Manila, with the meeting being attended by the Leaders of ASEAN Member States, the Prime Minister of Japan H.E. Sanae Takaichi, and Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn.

In the ASEAN leaders’ meeting today, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi pledged to work with ASEAN to boost regional economic and energy resilience to address export restrictions and vulnerabilities from rapid AI development, and strengthen supply chains, including on critical minerals.

A Japanese Foreign Ministry official said it was expected that Quad leaders would try to show unity, with maritime security, export restrictions, critical-minerals supply-chain diversification and AI among potential discussion points.
U.S. President Donald Trump is scheduled to arrive in China on Wednesday, for an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, following his meeting with the Quad leaders today.

This Quad alliance is heavily criticised by China, given that one of its purposes is to support Indo-Pacific nations in strengthening their sovereignty and simultaneously constrain China’s attempts to undermine that capacity-building.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to attend the Quad leaders’ meeting, the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit during his ongoing visit to the Philippines, External Affairs Ministry (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on Tuesday.

📰 ASEAN Summit LIVE updates: PM Modi to participate in ASEAN-India Summit; Quad meeting likely after President Trump arrives

In the first Quad Summit since 2024, PM Modi is expected to meet U.S. President Trump, Japanese PM Takaichi and Australian PM Albanese

“India, ASEAN represent around one-fourth of global population; it is important to decide our future by cooperation; not by competition,” PM Modi said in the India-ASEAN Summit in Manila today.

“We believe that India’s development and ASEAN’s prosperity are deeply interconnected,” he added.

The Embassy of India in Manila will resume all regular consular services, passport applications and visa processing from Wednesday, following a temporary suspension in view of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and East Asia Summit.

According to the earlier advisory, the closure was in accordance with Proclamation No. 1447 issued by the Government of the Republic of the Philippines, declaring special non-working days in the National Capital Region (NCR) for the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits.

Joint Statement of the 29th ASEAN-Japan Summit on Realising Economic Resilience was adopted today in Manila, with the meeting being attended by the Leaders of ASEAN Member States, the Prime Minister of Japan H.E. Sanae Takaichi, and Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn.

In the ASEAN leaders’ meeting today, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi pledged to work with ASEAN to boost regional economic and energy resilience to address export restrictions and vulnerabilities from rapid AI development, and strengthen supply chains, including on critical minerals.

A Japanese Foreign Ministry official said it was expected that Quad leaders would try to show unity, with maritime security, export restrictions, critical-minerals supply-chain diversification and AI among potential discussion points.

U.S. President Donald Trump is scheduled to arrive in China on Wednesday, for an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, following his meeting with the Quad leaders today.

This Quad alliance is heavily criticised by China, given that one of its purposes is to support Indo-Pacific nations in strengthening their sovereignty and simultaneously constrain China’s attempts to undermine that capacity-building.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to attend the Quad leaders’ meeting, the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit during his ongoing visit to the Philippines, External Affairs Ministry (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on Tuesday.

articles.title: What is Quad, what is on the Manila agenda, and why does the 2026 summit matter?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The summit in Manila will be the first meeting of Quad leaders since they gathered in Wilmington, United States, in September 2024

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will meet U.S. President Donald Trump, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at the Quad Summit to be held in Manila on the sidelines of the ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) meetings on November 17, 2026.

The summit in Manila will be the first meeting of Quad leaders since they gathered in Wilmington, United States, in September 2024. It will also be the first summit-level Quad meeting since Mr. Trump began his second term as U.S. President, and the first attended by Ms. Takaichi after assuming office as Japan’s Prime Minister. The previous Quad Leaders’ Summit was held in Wilmington in 2024, when Joe Biden was U.S. President and Fumio Kishida was Japan’s Prime Minister.

The Quadrilateral Security Dialogue, or Quad, brings together India, Australia, Japan and the United States. The grouping describes itself as a force for global good and is committed to promoting a free, open, inclusive, prosperous and resilient Indo-Pacific region. The Quad traces its origins to cooperation among the four countries in the aftermath of the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, when they coordinated relief and assistance efforts. Since then, it has developed a practical agenda covering health security, climate change, critical and emerging technologies, infrastructure and debt sustainability, cyber security, humanitarian assistance and disaster relief, and strengthening maritime domain awareness across the region.

Reuters, quoting officials during a briefing, reported that securing critical mineral supply chains and safeguarding commercial shipping routes for energy supplies would feature prominently on the agenda. “The issue of attacks on commercial ships is very likely to be taken up,” an official was quoted as saying. The safety of ships and seafarers is a matter of particular concern for India. At least 30 Indian seafarers aboard vessels operating in the Hormuz Strait , the Sea of Oman and the Black Sea have been killed in attacks linked to the conflicts involving Iran and Ukraine. Earlier reports had also suggested that leaders could announce a Quad Business Forum mechanism during the summit.

The leaders are also expected to deliberate on how the grouping can reaffirm its commitment to “a free and open Indo-Pacific that allows countries to develop resilience and strengthen capacity to determine their own paths”, a formulation contained in the joint statement issued after the Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting on May 26, 2026.

The Manila meeting will be the first Quad Summit hosted in a non-Quad country. It also reflects the difficulties India has faced as chair of the grouping in hosting a summit since cooperation was revived in 2017 and elevated to the leaders’ level during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021. Since then, India has not been able to host a Quad Leaders’ Summit, largely because of scheduling constraints involving the U.S. President. New Delhi is understood to be reluctant to pass on the chairship without first hosting a summit, and sources indicated that a meeting in Delhi next year remains a possibility, as per a report in The Hindu .

The Manila summit comes at a time when the Quad’s relevance is being closely watched amid protracted global conflicts, mounting pressure on supply chains and growing concerns over the security of major sea lanes. Several critical maritime choke points have become increasingly contested, while multilateral institutions such as the United Nations and the World Trade Organization have struggled to exert influence on major geopolitical disputes. At the same time, shifts in the global balance of power have intensified uncertainty. Against this backdrop, the Quad leaders are expected to discuss how the grouping can remain effective in addressing regional and global challenges.

While the Manila summit is significant for the Indo-Pacific grouping as it seeks to chart its future course, much of the international attention is likely to focus on Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen, China. There, on November 19, 2026, he is expected to participate in a three-way summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss a range of global issues, including nuclear arms control.

articles.title: Karnataka’s Minister assures translocation of 56 elephants in a month
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Residents of the affected areas say elephants began raiding crops and entering human habitats after the dam was built across the Hemavathi river in the 1970s

Minister for Excise K.M. Shivalinge Gowda, who is also Minister-in-charge of Hassan district, has said that the government of Karnataka will drive away 56 elephants roaming in parts of Belur taluk to the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary within a month.

Interacting with people staging a protest , blocking the Mudigere-Belur Road in Belur Town on Monday evening, the Minister said the State government, considering the incidents in the district, had taken a decision to capture and relocate 10 tuskers. “Now it has been decided to drive all 56 elephants roaming in the region out of the district to the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary,” he said.
Woman trampled to death by elephant in Hassan district in Karnataka
One more killed in elephant attack in Hassan’s Belur taluk; protests intensify
H.K. Suresh, Belur MLA, Shreyas Patel, MP, Former Minister B. Shivaramu and others were present.

Earlier, the Forest Department had permitted the capture and translocation of 10 male wild elephants. In an order dated November 16, the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (Wildlife) granted permission as per the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. The Wildlife Warden has directed the officials to carry out the operation using the kumki elephants from the elephant camps without delay.
Hassan district has been known for human-elephant conflict for decades, prompting the Forest Department to carry out major capture-and-translocation operations.

Residents of the affected areas say elephants began raiding crops and entering human habitats after the dam was built across the Hemavathi river in the 1970s. As the conflict intensified and protests followed, the first major operation was carried out in 1987-88, when 11 elephants were relocated.

The second major drive, in 2013-15, captured and relocated 22 problematic elephants. The department has also obtained special permission to capture and relocate troublesome elephants on several other occasions.

The department has now proposed a soft-release centre for elephants that stray into human habitats. It had earlier identified a part of the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary for the centre, but objections were raised because the site falls within the tiger reserve. An alternative location is now being considered.
