articles.title: As diabetes spikes in Kashmir, the health lens turns to the fabled wazwan
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Subsistence agriculture and labour-intensive living has been replaced by urbanisation and declining physical activity, while traditional dietary patterns persist largely unchanged, the doctor-authors of Diabetes Simplified for Kashmir say

The Kashmiri wazwan , an array of dishes adding up to 4,500-5,500 calories partaken during festivals and weddings, is one of the key cultural factors contributing to a spike in cases of diabetes in Kashmir, experts said.

Kashmir’s social life is organised around large, meat-centred feasts, most visibly the wazwan served at weddings or on Eid. Diabetes Simplified for Kashmir , a book released on World Diabetes Day (November 14), said the multi-course meal can run to over 30 mutton and chicken preparations, with the calorie intake “several times the average daily requirement”.

“Such exposure accumulates rather than occurs in isolation, and repeated post-prandial glucose and lipid excursions of this magnitude plausibly contribute to the region’s rising dysglycaemia burden,” the book, co-authored by endocrinologists Mohammad Hayat Bhat and Shahnawaz Mir, and cardiologist Nasir Shams, stated.
Degchis (traditional heavy-bottomed cooking pots) filled with wazwan dishes at a wedding feast in Srinagar. | Photo Credit: Reuters

J&K has witnessed a spike in the incidence of diabetes in the past three years. The Union Territory screened more than 2.15 million people for diabetes; 48,623 individuals have been diagnosed to have diabetes, according to data from the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. In 2025-2026, 2.84 million people were screened and 85,948 were found to have diabetes. “In the past three years, J&K added 2.18 lakh new patients to its diabetes burden,” the Ministry’s data suggested.
Apart from more universally seen factors, including poor physical activity and consumption of tobacco, the book identifies Kashmir’s unique lifestyle among the contributing factors.

“Kashmir’s daily plate remains rice-centric with rice typically supplying the bulk of meal volume and carbohydrate load. Large portions of rice translate directly into high postprandial glycaemic load,” it said.

“Type 2 diabetes prevalence in Kashmir has risen sharply within a single generation. A survey in 1999 found known diabetes in just 1.89% of adults, with 4.25% undiagnosed. Recent Indian Council of Medical Research-INDIA data show 7.8% prevalence,” the authors said, attributing the rising incidence of Type 2 diabetes to lifestyle in Kashmir.

The book noted that such a rapid shift cannot reflect genetic change. “It points instead to a compressed nutrition and lifestyle transition, as subsistence agriculture and labour-intensive living have been replaced by urbanisation and declining physical activity, while traditional dietary patterns — rice-centric meals, salt tea, preserved winter foods, and elaborate festive feasting — persist largely unchanged,” the experts said.

They also attributed the rise in cases of diabetes to Kashmir’s winters. “The glycaemic and fat load of the traditional meat and generous portion sizes do not act in isolation. Their convergence with a pronounced winter sedentary period appears to produce a compounding rather than merely additive metabolic burden across the Kashmiri annual cycle, in which periods of highest intake coincide with the lowest levels of expenditure,” they added.

articles.title: Police bust examination cheating racket in Jammu; 14 arrested
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Electronic devices, including wireless radio sets allegedly intended to facilitate the transmission of answers to candidates inside the examination halls, were found and seized by police

In a major intelligence-led operation, police on Sunday (November 15, 2026) arrested 14 suspected individuals for allegedly attempting to facilitate cheating in the Jammu and Kashmir Services Selection Board (SSB) Finance Assistant Examination in Jammu, an official said.

articles.title: Jawaharlal Nehru through an intelligence prism
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Critics of Jawaharlal Nehru have spared no effort to portray him as being rosy-eyed and naive about China; yet, memoirs of Bhola Nath Mullik, the intelligence chief who served under Nehru for almost the entire duration his Prime Ministership make it clear this was far from the truth

It is difficult to say or write anything about India’s first Prime Minister that has not already been said or written. What he comes across as when looked at through the prism of his intelligence chief is, however, a dimension of his working life that has not been adequately commented upon.

For almost the entire duration of his Prime Ministership, Jawaharlal Nehru’s intelligence chief was the redoubtable Bhola Nath Mullik who served as Director, Intelligence Bureau (DIB) from 1950 till shortly after Nehru’s demise. The Research and Analysis Wing (R&AW) had not yet come into existence then and the DIB was the last word on all matters pertaining to intelligence and security.
Political & National Report: Jawaharlal Nehru through an intelligence prism. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

articles.title: Carney says Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if Trump trade talks fail
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Mr. Carney said any Chinese investment would have to involve substantial manufacturing in Canada rather than simply assembling imported parts

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said that Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with U.S. President Donald Trump fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry.

“We have the best auto workers in the world, and we want them fully deployed, full opportunity, in an integrated North American market,” Mr. Carney told reporters in Cambodia. “That market has become less integrated because of U.S. trade actions.”

Mr. Carney said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) in Manila, Philippines, that any trade agreement with Washington must leave Canada with a viable auto industry. He said on Monday (November 16) that negotiations with the United States remain his priority, but their outcome could determine whether Canada pursues alternatives involving European, Chinese or Japanese automakers.
Asked whether potential Chinese investment was leverage in the U.S. negotiations, Mr. Carney replied: “It's not leverage. But action, reaction.”

“If they're not fully utilised in a North American context, that provides other opportunities,” Mr. Carney said of Canada's auto workers and manufacturing assets. “Canada is going to move forward either way.”

The Detroit Three — Ford, General Motors and Stellantis — operate factories across Canada, the United States and Mexico, with parts sometimes crossing borders multiple times before a vehicle is completed. Mr. Trump has repeatedly pushed automakers to move production to the United States from Canada.

Mr. Carney said any Chinese investment would have to involve substantial manufacturing in Canada rather than simply assembling imported parts. He said it would require proper labour standards, manufacturing facilities and domestic supply chains that expand over time, including Canadian critical minerals used in electric vehicles.
“It's not just about kit cars,” he said. “There has to be a manufacturing aspect involved.”

Under the January agreement, Canada reduced its 100% tariff on Chinese electric vehicles to 6.1%, initially allowing up to 49,000 vehicles annually, with the cap increasing over time. In exchange, China agreed to lower tariffs on Canadian agricultural products, including canola.
Mr. Carney said at the time that he expected the agreement to attract Chinese investment in Canada's auto industry and create jobs.

🌐 International & Geopolitics 📅 16 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Carney says Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if Trump trade talks fail

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Mr. Carney said any Chinese investment would have to involve substantial manufacturing in Canada rather than simply assembling imported parts

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said that Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with U.S. President Donald Trump fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry.

“We have the best auto workers in the world, and we want them fully deployed, full opportunity, in an integrated North American market,” Mr. Carney told reporters in Cambodia. “That market has become less integrated because of U.S. trade actions.”

Mr. Carney said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) in Manila, Philippines, that any trade agreement with Washington must leave Canada with a viable auto industry. He said on Monday (November 16) that negotiations with the United States remain his priority, but their outcome could determine whether Canada pursues alternatives involving European, Chinese or Japanese automakers.

Asked whether potential Chinese investment was leverage in the U.S. negotiations, Mr. Carney replied: “It's not leverage. But action, reaction.”

“If they're not fully utilised in a North American context, that provides other opportunities,” Mr. Carney said of Canada's auto workers and manufacturing assets. “Canada is going to move forward either way.”

The Detroit Three — Ford, General Motors and Stellantis — operate factories across Canada, the United States and Mexico, with parts sometimes crossing borders multiple times before a vehicle is completed. Mr. Trump has repeatedly pushed automakers to move production to the United States from Canada.

Mr. Carney said any Chinese investment would have to involve substantial manufacturing in Canada rather than simply assembling imported parts. He said it would require proper labour standards, manufacturing facilities and domestic supply chains that expand over time, including Canadian critical minerals used in electric vehicles.

“It's not just about kit cars,” he said. “There has to be a manufacturing aspect involved.”

Under the January agreement, Canada reduced its 100% tariff on Chinese electric vehicles to 6.1%, initially allowing up to 49,000 vehicles annually, with the cap increasing over time. In exchange, China agreed to lower tariffs on Canadian agricultural products, including canola.

Mr. Carney said at the time that he expected the agreement to attract Chinese investment in Canada's auto industry and create jobs.

articles.title: China confirms first Xi-Trump-Putin summit on November 19
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Chinese Foreign Ministry gave no further details including about what the topics of the historic meeting in the southern Chinese city would be
China confirmed that President Xi Jinping and his U. S. and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin will hold their first trilateral summit on Thursday (November 19, 2026) in Shenzhen.

“On November 19, Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-U.S. heads of state meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen,” the Foreign Ministry said in a brief statement on Monday (November 16, 2026).
It gave no further details including about what the topics of the historic meeting in the southern Chinese city would be.
It is expected to happen on the sidelines of a summit of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) and Thursday (November 19, 2026).
The Kremlin and the White House had both previously confirmed the three-way meeting.
Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals and is also set to bring up his war in Iran — but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said.
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said that in a recent meeting, Mr. Xi showed “irritation” when the idea of the trilateral talks covering Ukraine came up.
“He explicitly pointed out that this is a European conflict, in which the Europeans must also be at the table,” Mr. Steinmeier told ARD.
On nuclear disarmament, China has long insisted that the United States and Russia reduce their own giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its own stockpile.

articles.title: Violent protests erupt in Hasina’s hometown as tensions rise over her proposed return to Bangladesh
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government

Supporters of deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina ’s Awami League party staged violent demonstrations in her hometown of Gopalganj on Sunday (November 15, 2026), attacking police vehicles and installations amid growing political tensions over her stated plan to return to the country in December.
Editorial | In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties

The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government.

Ms. Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal in November 2025 for crimes against humanity over her government’s crackdown on protesters. She has rejected the charges and the proceedings.
Ms. Hasina, 79, has repeatedly said since July that she intends to return to Bangladesh in December and face legal proceedings, despite the death sentence against her.

The Bangladesh government has been seeking her extradition from India under a bilateral treaty. It has also declined a request made by a London-based law firm on Ms. Hasina’s behalf for a passport to facilitate her return.
Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that Bangladesh had completed the legal process to secure Ms. Hasina’s return and that the decision now rested with India.

Bangladesh has also linked progress on Ms. Hasina’s extradition to a possible visit to India by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman , saying her return and that of other fugitives sought by Dhaka would help create a conducive environment for the visit.
India has acknowledged receiving Bangladesh’s extradition requests but has not announced a decision.
On Friday (November 13, 2026), Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in New Delhi that Ms. Hasina’s extradition was a legal matter and would be dealt with accordingly.

articles.title: U.S. Treasury chief Scott Bessent wants answers soon from Nvidia
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: U.S. Treasury ‌Secretary Bessent said he wants to know if Nvidia used shell companies to dodge U.S. restrictions and sell its most powerful chips to China

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called on Nvidia on Sunday (November 15, 2026) to explain whether it knowingly allowed its most advanced AI chips to reach China, saying this was more important than ex-CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged spy for Beijing.

Speaking on “Fox News Sunday Morning Futures” three days after Mr. Huang resigned , Mr. Bessent said he wants to know if Nvidia used shell companies to dodge U.S. restrictions and sell its most powerful chips to China.

But late on Sunday (November 15, 2026), tech tycoon Elon Musk and several other Silicon Valley leaders added their signatures to more than 165,000 others on an open letter demanding that the company’s board members “bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts.”
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang misled top lawyer on affair with Alice Huang: report
Chinese company linked to Alice Huang obtained banned Nvidia chips: report
The United States forbids sales to China of the most cutting-edge AI chips, hoping to stay ahead of the Chinese in the race to dominate artificial intelligence.
In late 2025, President Donald Trump did authorize sales of Nvidia chips called H200s to the Chinese — but not the most advanced chips used to run AI models reshaping modern society.
“Nothing above the H200s can be sold to the Chinese,” Mr. Bessent said.
“What’s more important here,” he said, “is to examine whether Nvidia had a culture of compliance around the U.S. export restrictions.”
Mr. Bessent alluded to companies linked to Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center company that Huang’s alleged lover Alice Huang once worked for.

articles.title: Yemeni government forces retreat from strait in major setback in war against Houthis
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February

Yemeni government forces announced on Sunday (November 15, 2026) that they were withdrawing from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to focus on a defence of their ​main base in Aden, in a major setback for the Saudi-backed campaign against the Iran-aligned Houthis.

The announcement signalled the apparent ‌end of a six-week government counteroffensive to reclaim the coast near the mouth of the ​Red Sea, seized by the Houthis in September in a lightning advance that ⁠squeezed oil exports.

Sunday's announcement of a government retreat raises the prospect of new Houthi advances towards Aden, and underscores the predicament faced by Saudi Arabia in trying to stop the Houthis' drone and missile attacks on the kingdom. The government ‌forces have been based in Aden on the southern coast since 2015 after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa.

Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February.

"The Southern Armed Forces announce the ⁠implementation of a redeployment operation for its forces from Dhubab Airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area, west of Taiz Governorate," the main military force fighting for Yemen's government in the south of the country said in a statement.
"This step is taken based ​on the priority of securing the capital, Aden, ‌and the neighbouring governorates, as well as strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats."
There was no immediate response from the Houthis, or from Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government's main international ally.

Yemen's decade-long civil war, which had been dormant since 2022, abruptly reignited this summer as a ‌spillover from the Iran conflict. The Houthis made rapid gains to capture the coast along the ​Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which controls access to it, while besieging government forces in Taiz, the country's third-biggest city, in mountains above the approach to Aden.

A ⁠Saudi-backed government offensive last month rapidly retook key positions around the strait, notably Dhubab, but failed to drive the Houthis entirely away from the area or to retake the city of al-Mocha further up the coast.

The ‌Houthis have responded by intensifying drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia, grounding flights with strikes on its main airports as well as setting global energy markets on edge by targeting energy facilities.

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February

Yemeni government forces announced on Sunday (November 15, 2026) that they were withdrawing from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to focus on a defence of their ​main base in Aden, in a major setback for the Saudi-backed campaign against the Iran-aligned Houthis.

The announcement signalled the apparent ‌end of a six-week government counteroffensive to reclaim the coast near the mouth of the ​Red Sea, seized by the Houthis in September in a lightning advance that ⁠squeezed oil exports.

Sunday's announcement of a government retreat raises the prospect of new Houthi advances towards Aden, and underscores the predicament faced by Saudi Arabia in trying to stop the Houthis' drone and missile attacks on the kingdom. The government ‌forces have been based in Aden on the southern coast since 2015 after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa.

Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February.

"The Southern Armed Forces announce the ⁠implementation of a redeployment operation for its forces from Dhubab Airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area, west of Taiz Governorate," the main military force fighting for Yemen's government in the south of the country said in a statement.

"This step is taken based ​on the priority of securing the capital, Aden, ‌and the neighbouring governorates, as well as strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats."

There was no immediate response from the Houthis, or from Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government's main international ally.

Yemen's decade-long civil war, which had been dormant since 2022, abruptly reignited this summer as a ‌spillover from the Iran conflict. The Houthis made rapid gains to capture the coast along the ​Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which controls access to it, while besieging government forces in Taiz, the country's third-biggest city, in mountains above the approach to Aden.

A ⁠Saudi-backed government offensive last month rapidly retook key positions around the strait, notably Dhubab, but failed to drive the Houthis entirely away from the area or to retake the city of al-Mocha further up the coast.

The ‌Houthis have responded by intensifying drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia, grounding flights with strikes on its main airports as well as setting global energy markets on edge by targeting energy facilities.

articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Two celestial bodies—Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua—are a close pair of ancient quasars challenging ideas about early black hole growth

In the Hawaiian language, Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua means “two celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness in the brilliance of heat reincarnating energy into the universe”. It is a nickname astronomers have given to a strange new discovery: an unusual pair of quasars that are also closer to each other than thought possible.

A quasar is the extremely bright centre of a galaxy, where a black hole is drawing in and heating up gases, causing them to emit radiation. The pair is unusual because it existed when the universe was only 900 million years old.

The official designation of Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua is J1602+4228AB. Astronomers first spotted the brighter of the pair in 2004, and later the James Webb Space Telescope discovered the second one nearby. Finally, scientists used the Gemini North telescope in Hawaii to study both quasars together.
The quasars are separated by only 18,100 light-years, which is extremely tight for powerful objects of this nature.

Today, astronomers around the world are struggling to explain how black holes could have grown so large within the first billion years of the universe. The black hole in one of the quasars weighs a whopping 1.5 billion solar masses. One hypothesis is that young galaxies merged and funnelled copious amounts of gases towards their central black holes, feeding their growth.

Another is that the gravity of a galaxy lying between the earth and a quasar could bend the quasar’s light, making one object appear as two. This possibility remains to be eliminated — or confirmed — as astronomers continue studying Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua.

articles.title: Keralam’s orchids endure from highway trees to salt-sprayed shores
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A rescue-and-relocation project has saved over 27,000 native orchids from roadside trees felled in Keralam, and more than 71% were still alive, ​5,224 had flowered, and 1,934 had produced capsules after one to two years, offering a low-cost model for conservation
With their dazzling colours and ambrosial aromas, orchids are one of earth’s most distinctive flowering plant families.
They are found on every continent except Antarctica and count over 29,500 native species worldwide.
According to Orchids of India: A Pictorial Guide (2019), published by the Botanical Survey of India, Keralam accounts for more than a third of the 307 endemic orchids reported from India.
The State’s native orchid density is comparable to South American countries like Costa Rica, Viswambharan Sarasan, a research leader at the Royal Botanic Gardens in the U.K., said.
But habitat loss and fragmentation are increasingly threatening the State’s orchid diversity.
“As a child, I saw these orchids on coconut palms in our backyard [in Keralam],” he said. “But now they are disappearing from everywhere.”
However, according to Dr. Sarasan, relocating orchids from development sites or disturbed areas can reduce these losses.

Over the last three years, under Dr. Sarasan’s leadership, a research team at the KSCSTE-Malabar Botanical Garden and Institute for Plant Sciences in Calicut has rescued more than 27,000 native orchids growing on trees from being destroyed in road-widening activities in the State.

“I went to Kerala six, seven years ago, pitching this idea of growing orchids in large hubs where people congregate, such as the Napier Museum or the Kanakakunnu Palace in Thiruvananthapuram,” Dr. Sarasan, who hails from the capital city of Keralam, said.

With funding from the Royal Society International Exchanges programme, the project aimed to collect orchids from Keralam’s forests and rural areas. “However, we quickly realised there isn’t much diversity in the south,” he said.

He also visited and inspected the Basavanahalli residential school in the taluk.
Cauvery Neeravari Nigam superintending engineer Satish, assistant executive engineer Puttaswamy, tahsildar Ramesh and Public Works Department executive engineer Prabhu were among those present.

articles.title: Samples of 23 persons tested H5N1 negative, says Health Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: At least 16 poultry farms in Cuddalore district affected by Avian Influenza; continuous surveillance being done by the Public Health Department, says Arunraj

Minister for Health K.G. Arunraj on Monday said that samples of 23 persons, who are mostly poultry workers and veterinary staff in affected areas, have tested negative for Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (H5N1).

Addressing reporters on the sidelines of inspection of government hospitals in Vellore town, Dr. Arunraj said that 54 persons, who are mostly poultry workers and veterinary staff, were identified as these people were associated with affected poultry farms in Cuddalore. Of them, samples of 27 persons were collected and sent for testing. Results of 23 samples that have come so far have tested negative of H5N1 avian influenza virus. “The findings of 23 samples that were tested shows that the virus has not spread among humans. Despite sample results, surveillance has been intensified in affected areas,” he said.

The Minister further said that at least 16 poultry farms in Cuddalore district were affected with Avian Influenza (H5N1). The Department of Public Health has conducted 27 medical camps in a 10 kms radius of the affected farms as part of preventive measures. Continuous surveillance is also being done by the Public Health Department in coordination with the Department of Animal Husbandry, he said.

The Minister asserted that adequate stock of medicines especially anti-rabies and snake bites were available in government hospitals. The State government has also taken steps to fill around 2,500 vacant posts including pharmacists, doctors, nurses in government hospitals. The government has recently filled 4727 nurses in a transparent manner in the State. An order to fill vacant posts will be issued soon, he said.

Asked about setting up of new medical colleges in newly formed districts such as Ranipet, Tirupattur and Kallakuruchi, Mr. Arunraj said that the issue will be taken up to Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. Thereafter, necessary steps will be taken to set up new medical colleges in these new districts.

The Minister inspected Government Medical College Hospital and Pentland Government Multi speciality Hospital in Vellore town where he interacted with patients, hospital staff and health officials in the presence of Collector P.S. Leela Alex. Later, Mr. Arunraj attended the graduation ceremony at CMC in Vellore.

articles.title: GRAAM’s relocated head office inaugurated in Mysuru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The relocated head office is expected to serve as a platform for dialogue, collaboration and knowledge exchange among researchers, policymakers, academic institutions, development partners and community representatives
The relocated head office of Grassroots Research and Advocacy Movement (GRAAM) was inaugurated on its new premises on Vishwamanava Double Road in Kuvempunagar in Mysuru on Monday (November 16).

The relocated head office is expected to serve as a platform for dialogue, collaboration and knowledge exchange among researchers, policymakers, academic institutions, development partners and community representatives, according to a statement here by GRAAM, which is a not-for-profit public policy research and development think tank based out of Mysuru.

The inauguration, which was was done by T.S. Srivatsa, Krishnaraja MLA, was also marked by the unveiling of the GRAAM Journey Wall, titled ‘Sankalpadinda Sadhaneyedege’ (’From Resolve to Achievement’), showcasing the organisation’s 15-year journey, achievements and key milestones.

Mr. Srivatsa highlighted several priorities for Mysuru’s overall development. These included improving the city’s cleanliness, identifying a suitable site for the scientific disposal of animal carcasses, introducing effective measures for cattle dung management, and developing new tourism activities to attract visitors.

He called upon GRAAM to study local development challenges and opportunities, formulate suitable recommendations and action plans, and work towards their implementation through relevant government schemes. He also expressed his readiness to collaborate with GRAAM and extend the necessary support for initiatives contributing to Mysuru’s development.
Earlier, delivering the introductory remarks, GRAAM’s executive director Basavaraju R. Shreshta outlined GRAAM’s journey and its contributions across development sectors.

Established on January 12, 2011, GRAAM has worked to identify the needs, challenges and aspirations of rural communities through research and evidence-based studies, connecting grassroots voices with policymaking and governance, he said.

With a presence across 24 states and three Union Territories, the organisation works in areas including health, education, social security, rural development, livelihoods, local governance and youth leadership.

He described the relocation of the head office as a significant step in GRAAM’s growth, expressing confidence that the new premises would create further opportunities to expand its research, policy dialogue and development partnerships.

Srihari Dwarkanath, chairman of GSS Projects and Consultants Private Limited, pointed out that Mysuru was home to many thinkers, experts and individuals with innovative ideas, but needed appropriate platforms and mechanisms to translate their insights and suggestions into action.

articles.title: Maximise STP utilisation for ‘green water’ supply, says HMWSSB MD Ashok Reddy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a push to conserve groundwater and expand the use of treated wastewater, Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply & Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) Managing Director Ashok Reddy has directed officials to maximise the utilisation of Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) and strengthen the supply of ‘green water’ across the city.

During inspections of the Nagole and Patel Cheruvu STPs on Monday, he reviewed treatment operations, tanker filling facilities and the distribution of treated water, and instructed officials to ensure that STPs operate at their full capacity and to prepare detailed reports on engineering requirements, power consumption and operational costs.

At Patel Cheruvu, he joined local legislator Bandari Lakshma Reddy, and flagged off green water tankers and appealed to construction companies to use treated water instead of drinking water or groundwater for construction activities.

He also visited an apartment construction site, where he explored the feasibility of supplying treated water through dedicated pipelines. Officials were asked to identify large construction projects requiring water for at least two years and examine the possibility of laying 300–400 metre pipeline connections for continuous supply.

articles.title: Wholesale inflation rises to 12.3% in October 2026, second straight month of double-digit inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: According to economists, not only will this high wholesale inflation soon translate into higher consumer prices, but it also means an interest rate hike is nearly certain, which would dampen economic sentiment

Wholesale inflation in India surged to 12.3% in October 2026, the second consecutive month of double-digit inflation, official data released on Monday (November 16, 2026) showed. Fuel prices continue to be the main reason for the price rise, with the crude petroleum and natural gas sectors seeing inflation of more than 70%.

The new series of the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry has data that goes back to only April 2024 and so a historical analysis for a longer duration is not possible. However, the data shows that inflation in October was the highest since at least then.
This data follows the release of Consumer Price Index data last week that showed that even retail inflation had climbed above the Reserve Bank of India’s upper comfort mark of 6% in October 2026.
According to Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at the Bank of Baroda, it is only a matter of time before wholesale inflation translates into a further increase in the prices consumers pay.

“It has been seen that manufactured goods in particular have witnessed an increase of 9.5%, with high inflation rates in textiles, tobacco products, chemicals, rubber products, metals and electrical equipment,” Mr. Sabnavis pointed out. “This will pressurise companies into increasing their product prices at some point of time.”
“This passthrough will get reflected in the core part of the CPI in the coming months depending on the actions of industry,” he added.

Further, as Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive argues, the high WPI inflation makes a rate hike by the RBI in December a near certainty, which would have a further dampening effect on the economy.

“The sharp rise in WPI inflation to 12.39% in October 2026 reinforces the inflationary concerns already reflected in elevated retail inflation readings,” Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive said. “As a result, a rate hike by the RBI in the upcoming Monetary Policy Committee meeting [in December] now looks almost certain.”

“Higher interest rates may impact lending activity, investments, and consumption, while sentiment across the financial sector could remain under pressure,” Ms. Pandya added. “With geopolitical tensions resurfacing in the Russia-Ukraine region, risks to inflation and economic growth have become even more pronounced.”

Within the WPI, food inflation climbed to 8.3% in October 2026, the highest in 22 months. The overall fuel and power category saw inflation jump to nearly 33% in the same month, compared to about 26% in September 2026. These high levels were, however, also a result of a low base, since this segment of the WPI was in contraction for large parts of 2025.

articles.title: Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-producing states prompt concerns as India sets 2047 target
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.
The issue has come under judicial scrutiny, with both the Supreme Court earlier this month and the Odisha High Court in January flagging the underutilisation of mining capacities.

The Odisha High Court, while agreeing with petitioners who highlighted the sluggish operationalisation of mines despite environmental clearances, observed that the delay had resulted in an average annual revenue loss of ₹4,000 crore to the State.
However, industry sources, speaking on condition of anonymity, attributed the delays primarily to prolonged forest clearance procedures, which often exceed the stipulated 18-month timeframe.

Data cited by petitioner Citizens’ Action Forum (Bhubaneswar) show that of the 246 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of mining capacity granted environmental clearance in FY25, only around 159 MTPA had been operationalised.

Separately, data published by mining consultancy BigMint in June 2026 show that Odisha produced 158 MT of iron ore in FY26 against an environmentally cleared capacity of 278 MTPA, indicating capacity utilisation of nearly 60%.
The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, which is among the highest-grade varieties of iron ore

The shortfall also raises questions over India’s continued dependence on imports. According to the Mines Ministry, the country imported 12.3 MT of iron ore in FY26, incurring an expenditure of ₹11,115 crore.

Odisha accounted for more than 50% of India’s domestic iron ore production during FY26. Chhattisgarh contributed around 17.1%, followed by Karnataka at 16.6%. Capacity utilisation in the two states – albeit with significantly lower volumes than Odisha – stood at 62% and 80%, respectively, according to calculations based on BigMint data.

In January, the Odisha High Court directed that mining rights be mandatorily transferred to state-owned National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) to ensure “optimum utilisation of the mines” and “eradicate any burden on the government exchequer”.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance 📅 16 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.

The issue has come under judicial scrutiny, with both the Supreme Court earlier this month and the Odisha High Court in January flagging the underutilisation of mining capacities.

The Odisha High Court, while agreeing with petitioners who highlighted the sluggish operationalisation of mines despite environmental clearances, observed that the delay had resulted in an average annual revenue loss of ₹4,000 crore to the State.

However, industry sources, speaking on condition of anonymity, attributed the delays primarily to prolonged forest clearance procedures, which often exceed the stipulated 18-month timeframe.

Data cited by petitioner Citizens’ Action Forum (Bhubaneswar) show that of the 246 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of mining capacity granted environmental clearance in FY25, only around 159 MTPA had been operationalised.

Separately, data published by mining consultancy BigMint in June 2026 show that Odisha produced 158 MT of iron ore in FY26 against an environmentally cleared capacity of 278 MTPA, indicating capacity utilisation of nearly 60%.

The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, which is among the highest-grade varieties of iron ore

The shortfall also raises questions over India’s continued dependence on imports. According to the Mines Ministry, the country imported 12.3 MT of iron ore in FY26, incurring an expenditure of ₹11,115 crore.

Odisha accounted for more than 50% of India’s domestic iron ore production during FY26. Chhattisgarh contributed around 17.1%, followed by Karnataka at 16.6%. Capacity utilisation in the two states – albeit with significantly lower volumes than Odisha – stood at 62% and 80%, respectively, according to calculations based on BigMint data.

In January, the Odisha High Court directed that mining rights be mandatorily transferred to state-owned National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) to ensure “optimum utilisation of the mines” and “eradicate any burden on the government exchequer”.

articles.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security

Urgent pleas for cash from poor ​nations most exposed to the kind of climate-related disasters that have marked this year risk meeting a sluggish response at Turkiye’s COP31 talks as Western governments put ‌national security and living costs first.

Two years ago, rich countries agreed at UN climate talks they would triple ​climate funding for poorer countries to $300 billion per year by 2035 versus a previous 2020 target. Also by 2035, financing ⁠from all public and private sources combined would be $1.3 trillion annually.
The rich countries met their 2020 target two years late.

Since then, climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security.
Vulnerable small island nations say the cash they need to repair damage and to guard against future climate-related crises is again arriving too slowly and their own budgets have shrunk.

“Like many small island ‌developing states, we remain in a perpetual climate disaster recovery mode,” Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale told the conference. “We cannot build resilience ‌while ⁠our fiscal space erodes.”
Even when money is available, technical hurdles set by lenders can stretch the administrative capacity of ⁠small states.
For many developed nations, facing international and domestic unrest as citizens protest against the rising cost of living, their focus has narrowed.

Britain, which has sought to be a leader in addressing climate change, said in July savings made from switching some climate finance contributions from grants to loans would be used to help fund a cap on ​domestic bus fares.
The Stockholm ‌International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) estimated in April that world military expenditure reached $2.89 trillion in 2025, up 2.9% in real terms from 2024.

An Italian political leader's remarks criticising the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) during a recent event in India have drawn criticism in his country, with a senior leader of the ruling coalition in Rome saying it is “inappropriate” to intervene in a friendly nation's internal political debate.

articles.title: Beijing hails ‘groundbreaking significance’ of U.S., China, Russia summit in Shenzhen
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The meeting is likely to be more symbolic than substantial. U.S. officials have indicated that the agenda is the war in Ukraine, the situation in West Asia, including stabilising global energy supplies, and nuclear arms control

Thursday’s (November 19, 2026) summit meeting between the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia will be “of groundbreaking significance”, Beijing said on Monday (November 16, 2026), hailing the symbolism of a meeting of the three leaders taking place in China.
China’s Foreign Ministry said President Xi Jinping will host the summit with President Donald Trump and President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on November 19, on the sidelines of the APEC summit.

“The upcoming China-Russia-U.S. summit in Shenzhen will mark the first-ever face-to-face meeting among the heads of state of the three countries. The three leaders will exchange views in depth on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-country relations, and the meeting will be of groundbreaking significance,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said, adding that “strengthening communication, managing differences and stabilising relations among China, Russia and the U.S. serve the interests of all three countries”.

The meeting is likely to be more symbolic than substantial. U.S. officials have indicated that the agenda is the war in Ukraine, the situation in West Asia, including stabilising global energy supplies, and nuclear arms control. Whether there will be any concrete outcomes on any of those issues remains to be seen.

That has not, however, dampened enthusiasm in China, where state media has hailed the significance of the meeting. Beijing officially eschews references to a “G2” with the U.S. or a “G3” with the two countries and Russia, maintaining that it supports multipolarity. At the same time, the symbolism of China hosting the meeting has been seized upon to highlight Beijing’s global standing.

“The fact that China, Russia and the U.S. will sit down for face-to-face talks once again demonstrates that the head-of-state diplomacy plays an irreplaceable role in providing strategic guidance,” an editorial in the Global Times said. “The effort to foster a new type of major-country relationship marks a new phase in China’s major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics, featured by proactive leadership and systematic construction. The meeting to be held in Shenzhen is a manifestation of the international community’s high recognition of China’s image as a stable and responsible major country.”

Taking aim at naysayers, the editorial added that “those who view the trilateral meeting between China, Russia and the U.S. as major countries ‘carving out new spheres of influence’ or establishing a ‘new Yalta system’ clearly hold only a one-sided view of history, ignoring historical patterns.”

“They focus solely on the needs of individual parties while disregarding the overall and comprehensive interests, emphasise only the power aspect of major countries while neglecting their responsibilities, and are so preoccupied with the reality of polarisation in the international landscape that they lose sight of the ideal of democratising international relations,” it said.

Symbolism aside, few experts in China expect substantial outcomes amid what they acknowledge is growing strategic rivalry between China and the U.S. on the one hand, and an enduring rift between Russia and the West on the other, especially with the continuing war in Ukraine. Russia was “most enthusiastic” among the three for the summit, Su Liuqiang, a scholar at the Centre for American Studies at the Shanghai Institutes for International Studies, said in an interview with state media last week, adding that an informal exchange was likelier than a more structured, formal trilateral summit.

“On the one hand, there is substantial political resistance in the U.S.,” he said. “Anti-Russia sentiment remains strong in both the U.S. and among its European allies, with opposition to negotiating with Moscow while bypassing Ukraine and Europe. On the other hand, the three countries have differing priorities; Russia’s core concern is negotiations on a ceasefire in Ukraine, the U.S. is interested in the Russia-Ukraine conflict and non-proliferation, China supports peace talks but must also balance its relations with the U.S., Russia, Europe and Ukraine. In this context, a low-profile trilateral meeting is the more realistic option,” he added, noting that practical outcomes could emphasise stabilising global energy supplies.

articles.title: French troops deployed in Ukraine on secret mission: RFI
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The report did not say how many soldiers took part in the mission, which has been present in Ukraine since at least the summer of 2026

French soldiers have been operating in Ukraine for several months, training Ukrainian troops and helping maintain military equipment, Radio France Internationale (RFI) reported on Monday (November 16, 2026).

Citing sources, RFI said French lawmakers had not been informed of the deployment of the confidential mission, led by a French general and codenamed “Volia”, which can be translated as “freedom” and “will” from Ukrainian.
The report did not say how many soldiers took part in the mission, which has been present in Ukraine since at least the summer of 2026.
It described a “light and flexible” structure made up of “small teams deployed on short-term assignments”.

Several sources described as being familiar with the matter told RFI that an official “Gerfaut” mission in Poland serves as a cover for the presence of French troops in Ukraine and acts as a gateway for deployments into the country.
Gerfaut is a French military detachment deployed in Poland since 2023 as part of the European Union’s military assistance mission supporting Ukraine.
Under that framework, French army personnel are tasked with training officers who will go on to command Ukrainian combat units.
Since 2023, 25,000 Ukrainian soldiers have been trained by the French army, both in France and in Poland.
France will hold a two-round vote in April and May to elect a successor to President Emmanuel Macron, who has been a staunch supporter of Ukraine.

The far-right National Rally (RN) party, whose leader, Marine Le Pen, is the frontrunner to replace Macron, has said that France would cut financial aid to Ukraine within six months if she is elected President.

articles.title: 29-year-old regains limb movement after emergency stroke treatment at two govt. hospitals
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A 29-year-old woman from Manuguru, who was rushed to hospital after suddenly losing movement in her right arm and leg, regained significant mobility within hours after doctors at two government hospitals coordinated to administer emergency stroke treatment within the critical window.

Rajani’s ordeal began on an ordinary morning when she suddenly developed slurred speech and complete weakness on her right side. Recognising the signs of an acute stroke, doctors acted swiftly to prevent permanent brain damage.

She was first taken to Area Hospital, Manuguru, where Sai Kumar, a General Medicine specialist, identified the symptoms and arranged an urgent referral to Area Hospital, Bhadrachalam, nearly 60 km away, for emergency treatment.

Recognising the narrow window for intervention, M. Ramakrishna, medical superintendent of Area Hospital, Manuguru, coordinated directly with Tejaswi Gadde, physician at Area Hospital, Bhadrachalam, to facilitate her transfer.

At Bhadrachalam, doctors immediately conducted a CT scan to rule out bleeding in the brain before administering clot-dissolving medication. With Rajani still within the recommended 4.5-hour treatment window, doctors administered intravenous Tenecteplase at 2 p.m., around 3.5 hours after the symptoms began, said G. Ravi Babu, District Coordinator of Hospital Services (DCHS), Bhadradri Kothagudem.

The response to treatment was encouraging. Before the intervention, Rajani had no detectable movement in her right arm or leg, with her muscle power recorded at 0/5. Following thrombolysis, her muscle strength improved, and she regained the ability to move the affected limbs against resistance, though full strength is yet to return.

She remains under close neurological observation. The case also highlights the availability of advanced emergency treatment in government hospitals serving remote and tribal areas. The thrombolytic medication, which costs around ₹45,000 in the market, was administered to Rajani free of cost.

Dr. Ravi Babu appreciated the doctors, nurses and supporting staff at both hospitals for their prompt decisions and coordination. “Such interventions demonstrate how teamwork between government healthcare institutions can help deliver advanced, life-saving treatment even in geographically remote areas,” he said.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment 📅 16 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

🎯 Exam Relevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

A 29-year-old woman from Manuguru, who was rushed to hospital after suddenly losing movement in her right arm and leg, regained significant mobility within hours after doctors at two government hospitals coordinated to administer emergency stroke treatment within the critical window.

Rajani’s ordeal began on an ordinary morning when she suddenly developed slurred speech and complete weakness on her right side. Recognising the signs of an acute stroke, doctors acted swiftly to prevent permanent brain damage.

She was first taken to Area Hospital, Manuguru, where Sai Kumar, a General Medicine specialist, identified the symptoms and arranged an urgent referral to Area Hospital, Bhadrachalam, nearly 60 km away, for emergency treatment.

Recognising the narrow window for intervention, M. Ramakrishna, medical superintendent of Area Hospital, Manuguru, coordinated directly with Tejaswi Gadde, physician at Area Hospital, Bhadrachalam, to facilitate her transfer.

At Bhadrachalam, doctors immediately conducted a CT scan to rule out bleeding in the brain before administering clot-dissolving medication. With Rajani still within the recommended 4.5-hour treatment window, doctors administered intravenous Tenecteplase at 2 p.m., around 3.5 hours after the symptoms began, said G. Ravi Babu, District Coordinator of Hospital Services (DCHS), Bhadradri Kothagudem.

The response to treatment was encouraging. Before the intervention, Rajani had no detectable movement in her right arm or leg, with her muscle power recorded at 0/5. Following thrombolysis, her muscle strength improved, and she regained the ability to move the affected limbs against resistance, though full strength is yet to return.

She remains under close neurological observation. The case also highlights the availability of advanced emergency treatment in government hospitals serving remote and tribal areas. The thrombolytic medication, which costs around ₹45,000 in the market, was administered to Rajani free of cost.

Dr. Ravi Babu appreciated the doctors, nurses and supporting staff at both hospitals for their prompt decisions and coordination. “Such interventions demonstrate how teamwork between government healthcare institutions can help deliver advanced, life-saving treatment even in geographically remote areas,” he said.

articles.title: Pollution in Yamuna increased despite huge expenditure on cleaning: Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: “This court is of the opinion that everything that is wrong with the civic administration in towns, cities and villages situated along the banks of the river is reflected in the poor health of the river and in the 520 drains that discharge wastewater into the Yamuna,” said SC

Pollution in Yamuna has only increased despite huge sums being spent on cleaning the river, the Supreme Court has said, directing the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) to monitor water quality at the points where the Yamuna and its major drains enter and exit states, Union territories and districts.

In an order dated November 4, a Bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Manmohan observed that industrial pollutants and untreated sewage must be stopped at the source, and merely constructing more sewage treatment plants is not sufficient to clean the river.

"This court is of the opinion that everything that is wrong with the civic administration in towns, cities and villages situated along the banks of the river is reflected in the poor health of the river and in the 520 drains that discharge wastewater into the Yamuna. This is why, despite huge sums being spent on cleaning the river, pollution in the Yamuna has only increased," the Bench said while hearing a plea related to cleaning of the river.
The top court said industrial pollution and untreated sewage must be curtailed, if not stopped altogether, at the source.

"Where that is not possible, the sewage must first be tapped and then treated. However, tapping will remain a challenge in absence of a robust sewage system and due to joining of stormwater and sewage drains.

"This court is further of the opinion that it would be difficult, if not impossible, for civic authorities to tap sewage in most illegal and unauthorised colonies built on encroached land, since they have not been built on a grid layout and have hardly any space for laying a sewage system," it said.

The apex court said unless illegal and unauthorised colonies and 'jhuggi-jhopdi' (slum) clusters on the drains as well as on the river bed are removed, with rehabilitation of their occupants, their sewage will continue to pollute the river.
The court directed that if water quality deteriorates while passing through a particular state, Union territory or district, the concerned authorities would be held accountable and penalised.
ALSO WATCH Every Chhath, the same question returns: Why is the Yamuna still polluted?

"If the water quality deteriorates on any parameter while flowing through, or exiting a state/Union territory or a district therein, that state/Union territory or district... shall be held accountable and penalised. The said compensation/ fine shall be deposited with the registry of this court," the Bench said, directing CPCB to suggest a formula for calculating the said compensation.

articles.title: India scrutinises Red Bull’s sugar levels as ‘energy drink’ dispute escalates
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The basis and nature of the energy-related positioning of the product require scientific and regulatory substantiation, the FSSAI said in the document

India is scrutinising the composition of Red Bull, the drink made by the eponymous Austrian company, warning the product’s “energy drink” label could encourage people to consume too much added sugar, an official notice showed, opening a new front in the regulator’s fight over food safety standards.

It is the first time India has raised health concerns and questioned companies on the ingredients of their energy drinks in a dispute that began in June and has triggered legal challenges in the Delhi High Court.

In a confidential notice to Red Bull on Monday, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) targeted the drink’s “nutritional composition”, saying it derived a significant proportion of its declared energy from the “substantial” amount of added sugar.
“The basis and nature of the energy-related positioning of the product require scientific and regulatory substantiation,” the FSSAI said in the document, which was reviewed by Reuters.

The notice gives Red Bull seven days to explain why India should not prohibit its use of the “energy drink” label given it had the “potential to mislead consumers and encourage excessive consumption of added sugar.”
Red Bull and the FSSAI did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

India’s energy drinks market is set to be worth $1.6 billion by 2028, with sales growing 12.6% annually, faster than in the US and China, according to Euromonitor. Red Bull’s India revenue stood at $130 million in 2024, more than double the earnings recorded four years ago.

Health experts are concerned energy drinks contain high levels of sugar, caffeine and taurine, an amino acid that research suggests can contribute to health problems. The drinks will be banned for under-16s in England from April next year.

In court in recent weeks, Red Bull, PepsiCo, Monster Beverage and Reliance Consumer have challenged the June order banning the label “energy drinks”, saying they were not given any advance notice of the strict action.

However, while Red Bull managed to secure a temporary court injunction to enable it to continue using the “energy drink” label, its competitors were told that once they sold their existing stock they had to stop using the label.

It is the first time India has raised health concerns and questioned companies on the ingredients of their energy drinks in a dispute that began in June and has triggered legal challenges in the Delhi High Court.

In a confidential notice to Red Bull on Monday, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) targeted the drink’s “nutritional composition”, saying it derived a significant proportion of its declared energy from the “substantial” amount of added sugar.

“The basis and nature of the energy-related positioning of the product require scientific and regulatory substantiation,” the FSSAI said in the document, which was reviewed by Reuters.

The notice gives Red Bull seven days to explain why India should not prohibit its use of the “energy drink” label given it had the “potential to mislead consumers and encourage excessive consumption of added sugar.”

Red Bull and the FSSAI did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

India’s energy drinks market is set to be worth $1.6 billion by 2028, with sales growing 12.6% annually, faster than in the US and China, according to Euromonitor. Red Bull’s India revenue stood at $130 million in 2024, more than double the earnings recorded four years ago.

Health experts are concerned energy drinks contain high levels of sugar, caffeine and taurine, an amino acid that research suggests can contribute to health problems. The drinks will be banned for under-16s in England from April next year.

In court in recent weeks, Red Bull, PepsiCo, Monster Beverage and Reliance Consumer have challenged the June order banning the label “energy drinks”, saying they were not given any advance notice of the strict action.

However, while Red Bull managed to secure a temporary court injunction to enable it to continue using the “energy drink” label, its competitors were told that once they sold their existing stock they had to stop using the label.

articles.title: Study provides atlas of links between early-life environmental exposures, health
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The authors "identified a set of 'master regulator' exposures, such as maternal smoking, indoor air pollution, endocrine-disrupting chemicals, and dietary and urban factors, that influenced multiple health domains, with effects persisting into adolescence"

Environmental exposures during pregnancy and childhood, including tobacco smoke, indoor air pollution and dietary quality, may be associated with health outcomes such as BMI and behaviour, with many of these links persisting into adolescence, a new study has found.

Researchers, led by those at the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal), identified six prenatal and 42 childhood exposures associated with multiple outcomes and health families simultaneously.

The study, published in Science Advances , provides an atlas of associations between early-life environmental exposures and health, highlighting factors that may be relevant for prevention and policy action.

"Our approach allowed us to jointly analyse associations between the early-life exposome and multiple health outcomes instead of studying each one separately," first author Augusto Anguita-Ruiz, ISGlobal and University of Barcelona researcher, said.
The researchers used an outcome-wide exposome approach to study associations of exposures with health across four domains -- cardiometabolic, mental health, respiratory, and allergic problems.
The exposome refers to the totality of environmental exposures a person experiences throughout life, including factors such as diet, tobacco smoke and air pollution.

The exposures examined included diet, physical activity, sleep and other individual behaviours, as well as tobacco smoke, indoor and outdoor air pollution, chemical pollutants, metals and characteristics of the built environment.

The authors "identified a set of 'master regulator' exposures, such as maternal smoking, indoor air pollution, endocrine-disrupting chemicals, and dietary and urban factors, that influenced multiple health domains, with effects persisting into adolescence."

Senior co-author Valérie Siroux, researcher at the French National Institute for Health and Medical Research (Inserm), said: "Although no exposure was associated with all four domains, around one in three of the selected exposures was linked to more than one, suggesting that certain exposures can have broad and multisystemic effects on health."

Maternal smoking during pregnancy was associated with higher BMI and more externalising behaviours, such as aggression and impulsivity, in children during both early childhood and adolescence, as well as more ADHD symptoms during adolescence.

articles.title: WHO sounds the alarm on antimicrobial resistance threat
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Only 42 countries -- less than one in five -- had a national action plan on AMR that was financed, implemented and monitored, according to the World Health Organization

The spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is threatening modern medicine despite progress in combating drug-resistant bacteria, senior World Health Organization officials said Monday, November 16, 2026.
WHO officials said countries had expanded efforts to tackle AMR, but warned that progress in prevention, diagnosis and the appropriate use of antibiotics remained too slow to meet global targets.
Bacteria have long evolved resistance to medicines designed to kill them.
The widespread use of antibiotics in human health, animal husbandry and food production has accelerated the problem, making AMR one of the leading causes of infectious-disease deaths worldwide.

"Antimicrobial resistance is widespread and threatening the future of modern medicine," said Jean-Pierre Nyemazi, interim head of antimicrobial resistance at the WHO. "Unlike COVID-19, which was very visible, drug-resistant infections have been taking people's lives for years without us noticing it and raising the alarm as we should," said Nyemazi.
In 2021 alone, AMR was directly responsible for more than one million deaths and linked to some 4.7 million others, said the agency.

A WHO investigation in 183 countries into the progress of the fight against antimicrobial resistance this year revealed that nearly nine countries in 10 had a national action plan against the phenomenon. In 2017, the figure was only around four in 10.
But only 42 countries -- less than one in five -- said they had a plan that was financed, implemented and monitored, said Pravasha Prakash, an AMR technical officer with the global health agency.
"Countries are moving forward in every step but progress still needs to be speeded up to reach the 2030 targets," she added.

One of the main weaknesses remains access to diagnostics. Only 36% of countries had a national reference laboratory capable of testing for resistance in all bacteria and fungi monitored by the WHO -- well short of the 80% target set for 2030.

fullParagraphs: Hridayam is a social campaign to raise awareness about cardiovascular health and prevention among young people

Shaastra 2027, the annual techno-managerial festival of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Madras, has launched Hridayam, a social campaign to raise awareness about cardiovascular health and prevention among young people.

The initiative, in collaboration with Cardiac Wellness Institute, began with a session on stress management for students, led by Priya Chockalingam, clinical director of the institute. The session covered the effects of acute and chronic stress on heart health and practical approaches to managing stress. A pre-session assessment found that academic workload, extracurricular activities, and job placement concerns were major sources of stress among students.

Students also visited the institute to interact with patients undergoing cardiac rehabilitation and learn about the role of diet, physical activity, sleep and stress management in maintaining heart health. The campaign will conclude during Shaastra, scheduled from January 2 to 6, 2027, with heart health screenings for visitors.

articles.title: Trump says ‘would not mind’ Huang being reinstated at Nvidia
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Trump said Jensen Huang ‘learned a big lesson’ and he ‘would certainly not mind’ if he was reinstated, while adding that there’s a ‘big group of people that would like him to return’

Jensen Huang is reportedly trying to make a comeback as CEO of Nvidia as a campaign to reinstate him picked up steam Monday, with support from tech industry leaders as well as many of the chipmaker's employees.

U.S. President Donald Trump, who has been close with Mr. Huang, also suggested he could return to Nvidia. Mr. Trump said Mr. Huang “learned a big lesson” and he “would certainly not mind” if he was reinstated.
There’s a “big group of people that would like him to return,” Mr. Trump added.
SpaceX and Tesla boss Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, CEO of video game maker Epic Games, were among thousands of people who signed an online petition calling for Huang to return to the company.

Mr. Huang resigned last week from Nvidia, apparently ousted by the board after revelations that he had extramarital affairs, both with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of being an intelligence asset for Beijing and with a senior executive who reported to him. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has stepped in as interim CEO while the board searches for a replacement.

Mr. Huang is plotting a comeback, the Financial Times reported over the weekend, citing multiple anonymous sources. The newspaper said he has been discussing the possibility with confidants, as his allies assembled a “war room” of Silicon Valley allies to lobby for his return.

The “Stand with Jensen” petition was set up Friday (November 13) and soon gathered momentum, gaining signatures from current and former Nvidia staff, investors and other supporters. It calls on the board to bring back Mr. Huang while an independent investigation proceeds or there's “compelling evidence” that his departure is in the company's best interests.

“We are concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process,” the petition's organizers said in an open letter. “We do not have access to the Board's private deliberations. We have not been shown evidence substantiating the allegation that the woman at the center of this controversy was a spy.”
The identities of the signatories could not be independently verified, and the website said that their “affiliations are self-reported and not verified.”
Some people posted on their personal accounts that they supported the effort.

articles.title: India and Egypt form working group to explore trade deal contours
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: India and Egypt have agreed to establish a joint working group to explore the Terms of Reference (ToR) for a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement between the two countries, the government announced on Monday (November 16, 2026).

During his ongoing visit to Egypt, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal co-chaired, along with Egypt’s Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade Mohamed Farid Saleh, the 7th session of the India-Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC) in Egypt’s New Administrative Capital.
This was the first time this JTC has been convened at the ministerial level.

“As a key outcome of the 7th Joint Trade Committee meeting, both Ministers agreed to establish a Joint Working Group to explore the Terms of Reference for a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement to facilitate stronger bilateral trade, improve access to both markets and promote investment linkages between the two countries,” the government said in a release.
The release also said that both sides reaffirmed their commitment to expanding bilateral trade, with a target of $12 billion.

“Egypt’s proximity to the Suez Canal and its connectivity with African, Arab and European markets make it a valuable partner for export-oriented manufacturing and regional supply chains,” the release said.
“India, in turn, offers Egyptian investors and exporters a large and dynamic market, increasingly competitive infrastructure and opportunities for technology and production partnerships,” it added.

The committee also reviewed the growth in India-Egypt trade, which increased by 35% to $6.5 billion in 2025-26. Trade during the first half of the current financial year (April-September 2026) also stood at a little more than $5 billion, up 65% over its level in the same period of 2025.

articles.title: Divergent positions mark draft text of COP31 under way in Turkiye
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Developing countries call for developed nations to lead emissions cuts and climate finance efforts

Developing countries have called on developed nations to take the lead in achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 and net-negative emissions by 2045, as divergent positions emerged in the draft cover text at the ongoing COP31 climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkiye.

Net zero refers to balancing the amount of carbon dioxide emitted with the amount removed from the atmosphere. Several developed countries have set 2050 targets for achieving net-zero emissions, while major developing economies such as India and China have committed to targets of 2070 and 2060, respectively.

The positions of developing countries are largely represented by coalitions such as the Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDC), which includes India, the Arab Group, the African Group and the Least Developed Countries (LDCs).
Developed-country positions are primarily represented by the European Union, the United Kingdom and Japan. The United States has withdrawn from the Paris Agreement.

The draft cover text also includes a proposal asking developing countries to contribute voluntarily towards climate finance. This funding is intended to help countries adapt to a fossil-fuel-free economy and address losses and damage caused by climate change.

Under the UN climate framework, developed countries, which bear greater historical responsibility for accumulated carbon emissions, are expected to support developing countries through finance and technology as they pursue lower-emission development pathways.

Developing countries have also called for the elimination of measures such as the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) by the end of 2027. The mechanism imposes a tariff on certain imports, including steel, based on the carbon emissions generated during production. Developing countries argue that such measures disadvantage their industries, which often have lower production costs but higher emissions.

Another proposal in the draft concerns a target to source 35% of energy use from electricity by 2035. Some countries have called for there to be no obligation to meet this goal, which was proposed by the COP31 presidency.

COP31 president of negotiations Chris Bowens said the first draft was intended to incorporate proposals from all parties, acknowledging that countries would disagree on certain elements. He said the draft had been released early to ensure transparency and reflect the range of positions.

Andreas Sieber, head of political strategy at activist group 350.org, called for a transition towards renewable energy and electrification, supported by adequate funding. He said the credibility of the climate negotiations depended on leadership in moving away from fossil fuels.

A U.S. official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive military operations, on Monday (November 16, 2026) confirmed the carrier’s arrival in the region.
