The Roosevelt, along with its accompanying strike force, left San Diego in September.

The Theodore Roosevelt joins the USS George H.W. Bush and the USS George Washington aircraft carriers, as well as scores of smaller navy ships, that are in the region maintaining a blockade of Iranian shipping. The H.W. Bush arrived in the region in April while the George Washington arrived in August.
According to the Navy, the flotilla in the Arabian Sea now includes three aircraft carriers as well as 13 destroyers, two cruisers and a littoral combat ship.

articles.title: After Yemen setback, Saudi Arabia replaces military commander
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Houthis have made rapid gains ⁠against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government since the U.S.-Iran conflict reignited Yemen’s frozen civil war this summer, drawing Riyadh back into confrontation with the group

Saudi Arabia replaced the commander overseeing its coalition against Yemen’s Iran-allied Houthis ‌on Monday (November 16, 2026) after Riyadh’s Yemeni allies were forced to withdraw from swathes of territory in ​a major setback for their campaign against the group.

The Houthis have made rapid gains ⁠against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government since the U.S.-Iran conflict reignited Yemen’s frozen civil war this summer, drawing Riyadh back into confrontation with the group.

After gaining ground in a counter-attack in October, the Yemeni government said on Sunday (November 15, 2026) it was withdrawing from ‌areas near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a global shipping artery, to focus on defending its base of operations in Aden, a port city on the southern coast.

People in the Yemeni military ‌said on Monday (November 16, 2026) the Houthis had advanced to the southern coastal area of Khor Omairh, ‌some ⁠100 km (62 miles) west of Aden and were 25 km (16 miles) from government lines at Qawah, ⁠another coastal area.
A royal decree issued by Saudi Arabia’s King Salman spelt out changes to the command of the Saudi-led coalition.

The existing commander, Lieutenant General Fahd bin Hamad Al-Salman, was appointed as adviser to the defence minister for military affairs, while Chief of ​the General Staff General Fayyad Al-Ruwaili was assigned ‌the additional role of commanding the joint forces, Saudi state media reported.
Two Western diplomats linked the change directly to battlefield developments in Yemen and the Houthi advance.
The Saudi government media office didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
The Houthis have been firing ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports and ‌oil facilities since the Yemen war restarted.
Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on ​Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping have enhanced Iran’s position in the wider Middle East conflict.

articles.title: AIIMS Delhi performs a life-changing spinal repair in utero, before the patient’s first breath
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: This is India’s first open foetal repair for myelomeningocele, a defect in which the spinal cord and its coverings protrude through an opening in the spine; over 30 clinicians and nurses involved in multidisciplinary procedure

The All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Delhi has performed India’s first open foetal repair of a lumbosacral myelomeningocele — the most severe form of spina bifida — at 25 weeks’ gestation.

“The six-hour operation repaired the cerebrospinal-fluid-leaking lumbosacral defect in utero. It followed more than five weeks of multidisciplinary planning, detailed foetal imaging, non-directive counselling, anaesthetic preparation, and operative simulation,’’ AIIMS said in a statement.
A myelomeningocele is an open neural tube defect in which the spinal cord and its coverings protrude through an opening in the spine.

The patient was first screened and counselled by K. Aparna Sharma from the Maternal–Fetal Medicine team. The multidisciplinary procedure was performed using high-end microscopy and continuous high-end ultrasonography assistance at the Neurosciences Centre. The procedure was provided free of cost to the family under the Union government’s Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK).

Deepak Gupta, who led the neurosurgical component, said that the intervention was done after rigorous selection. “Prenatal repair seeks to limit ongoing injury to exposed neural tissue, reduce the subsequent need for cerebrospinal-fluid diversion for hydrocephalus, and improve selected neurological outcomes. It is not a cure, and long-term multidisciplinary care remains essential,” he said.

More than 30 clinicians and nurses from the Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Maternal–Fetal Medicine, Neurosurgery, Obstetrics and Neuroanaesthesia, Plastic Surgery, Radiodiagnosis, Neonatology, and Nursing teams of the Neurosciences Centre and Obstetrics–Gynaecology services participated in the procedure.

Professor Aparna Sharma added that this foetal intervention was well-reasoned and a planned decision aimed to optimise the outcomes of both the baby and the mother. The safety of both mother and foetus was ensured through detailed counselling, high-quality anaesthesia, and coordinated surveillance before and after surgery.

“International trial evidence supports prenatal repair in carefully selected foetuses with open myelomeningocele. The procedure nevertheless carries important maternal and foetal risks, including prematurity and uterine-scar complications, and must be performed only in specialised centres,’’ she said.

The team emphasised that foetal surgery is a treatment for selected pregnancies, not a substitute for prevention. Neural-tube closure occurs by approximately 28 days after conception, often before pregnancy is recognised. Pre-conception folic-acid counselling, evidence-based food fortification with folates, and robust national surveillance remain essential to reducing India’s burden of neural tube defects.

“The mother and foetus will continue to receive close multidisciplinary surveillance through pregnancy, delivery, and the newborn period,’’ the AIIMS statement said, adding that a child with spina bifida may begin life with paralysis, hydrocephalus, and lifelong challenges.

articles.title: Matrescence: when motherhood needs mental health support
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: At least one in five women will experience mental health problems during pregnancy until till the first year after childbirth. This cannot be ignored any longer: we need better, more comprehensive policies and programmes to support mothers during this vulnerable period

Monica was not prepared for a caesarean section. She had done everything right and had been assured of a vaginal delivery. Then two weeks before the expected date of delivery, she had to be rushed to the emergency for a caesarean. Monica felt that she had completely lost control of the situation. She found herself alone in an intensive care ward away from her baby, who was in the neonatal ICU and described her birth experience as being extremely traumatic. She is now unable to bond with her baby and keeps questioning herself. Am I such a terrible mother? Will I be like this lifelong?

Priya became pregnant after multiple IVF procedures but did not disclose the pregnancy to anyone till the third trimester, as she didn’t want to jinx it. After a healthy baby girl was born, Priya continued to be anxious and could not trust anyone else to take care of the baby. She would be hypervigilant, and even the smallest change in the infant’s spit-up or breathing would make her panic.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Restoration of Statehood is essential for peace in Jammu and Kashmir

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Three months of lull established by security forces in Jammu and Kashmir was rattled by the back-to-back incidents of violence in the past six days. On November 11, a terror attack on a checkpoint manned by the personnel of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in Kulgam left three jawans injured. On November 16, a local, whom the police suspected of having joined the terror ranks a few days ago, was killed after six days of a siege-like anti-terror operation in residential areas of Kulgam. In Jammu’s Kishtwar, two Special Police Officers (SPOs) of the J&K Police were found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they were reported missing in a forest range on November 11. The police and the Army, however, remain tight-lipped about the circumstances around the killing of these SPOs, and there are conflicting reports on the circumstances that led to their deaths. The anti-terror operation in civilian areas of Kulgam has raised concerns. Former J&K Chief Minister and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti described the operation, spread over six days, as “collective punishment that only breeds alienation and resentment,” while NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar suggested that entire villages were put under prolonged restrictions for days. The Omar Abdullah government , because of limited powers and no jurisdiction over the police in J&K, a Union Territory since 2019, finds itself hamstrung. The iron hand policy to stamp out terrorism and separatism has been effective from a strictly security perspective — terror attacks as well as local recruitments into terror ranks have declined. According to the police, local recruits have come down to single digit or fewer than 10 in Kashmir.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Editorial Context: Elusive peace: On Kashmir terror attack. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

optsMr: All-too fallible: On India’s vote against moratorium on death penalty
dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Death penalty requires a near-infallible criminal justice system

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India’s vote against a proposed global moratorium on the death penalty at the UN is consistent with its position at the forum; it has defended its retention of the penalty as a sovereign decision backed by judicial safeguards, including the “rarest of rare” condition and sessions courts’ sentences requiring a High Court’s confirmation. At the same time, the Supreme Court has increasingly restricted capital punishment and research has failed to find evidence of additional deterrence over life imprisonment . India’s distinction between judicial executions and extrajudicial killings is legally valid but its further claim that due process protects people facing execution is less so. While India last executed convicts in 2020, for the Delhi gang-rape and murder, Parliament expanded the number of capital offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — a form of penal populism that projects the political attractiveness of the state’s response to public outrage, especially in cases of sexual violence, without addressing the poor policing and low conviction rates that actually undermine deterrence . The country had 574 people on death row on December 31, 2025, the highest since 2016, thanks to trial court rulings, challenging claims about judicial safeguards in practice. The report of the 2015 Law Commission headed by Justice A.P. Shah said the death penalty “fails to achieve any constitutionally valid penological goals” and recommended abolishing it for all crimes except terrorism and waging war.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: prison / judiciary (system of justice) / crime, law and justice / United Nations / death penalty policies

optsMr: Outlook outage: On Microsoft and dangers of centralising digital systems
dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The dangers of centralising the internet’s architecture are now clear

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Editorial Context: Outlook outage: On Microsoft and dangers of centralising digital systems. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While maintaining its hard stance on cross-border terrorism, India has an opportunity to recognise that many of its other interests still merit sustained cooperation with Pakistan as the latter’s climate minister Musadik Masood Malik prepares to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. India’s official position since the Pahalgam attack and the ensuing confrontations along the border is that terrorism and bilateral talks cannot coexist. A month later, Prime Minister Narendra Modi signalled that India’s relations with Pakistan would remain subordinate to its demands on cross-border terrorism by extending the condition to trade and water. South Asia is already one of the least economically integrated regions worldwide, with intra-regional trade at around 5%, and, as Chatham House has inferred, strained ties between India and its neighbours have created diplomatic vacuums that Beijing has taken advantage of through trilateral and regional groupings. Now, by inviting all SCO members to the national capital and participating in meetings ahead of the August 2027 Islamabad Summit, New Delhi has shown some maturity as a convening power. Islamabad is also being pragmatic in keeping channels open during its SCO chairmanship by participating in an initiative championed by Mr. Modi.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Before the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. President Donald Trump had repeatedly threatened to “destroy” Iran unless it entered into a deal with the U.S. to end the war. Since the elections, in which Mr. Trump’s Republican Party suffered a massive defeat , the U.S. President appears to have toned down his rhetoric. Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. The U.S. and Israel carried out heavy bombing for 40 days but achieved none of their declared objectives. There is no guarantee that another round of strikes would force Iran to change its position. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. With discontent rising against the BJP, which still occupies a hegemonic position in the party system , the Opposition feels a wind behind its sails, and its major parties agree that the only way to take on the BJP is a formidable coalition with a compelling, unified message. But the Congress’s attempt to rebuild itself in the Hindi heartland and in States where it once held sway has strained that unity. In Bihar, the Mahagathbandhan failed to reap the benefits of anti-incumbency against the Janata Dal (United)-BJP alliance, partly because it could not tap the full support of the social forces behind the Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Congress, and partly because the Congress took too long to settle seat-sharing for the campaigns to gel. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners.
